qcR1vctbGZ.one_liner: Projection-free constrained optimization step minimizing a linear function over the constraint set intersected with a ball around the iterate
qcR1vctbGZ.problem: Projected gradient descent requires projections onto the constraint set, which can be expensive, and a projection-free analogue with comparable convergence theory is missing.
qcR1vctbGZ.method: BroxGD replaces the proximal backward step of forward-backward methods with the broximal operation, so each step minimizes the linear function of the gradient over the constraint set intersected with a ball of radius t_k around the current iterate. The paper develops convergence theory across a wide range of optimization regimes and radius rules, including a backtracking rule.
qcR1vctbGZ.key_idea: Replace projection with a linear minimization oracle restricted to the intersection of the constraint set and a ball centered at the current iterate.
qcR1vctbGZ.evidence: Convergence theory spanning a wide range of regimes and radius rules; the contribution is stated as theoretical, with toy experiments and potential applications as illustration.
qcR1vctbGZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clearly written and well positioned as an in-between of projected gradient descent and Frank-Wolfe, with a comprehensive convergence theory.
qcR1vctbGZ.main_concern: Practical usefulness is unclear because closed-form iterates for interesting constraint sets are not derived, a radius must be supplied at every iteration, and the experiments are limited.

pt14gnV3dl.one_liner: Mini-batch k-means with exponential-moving-average centroid updates and fitted scaling laws for decay rate and batch size.
pt14gnV3dl.problem: Lloyd's k-means needs many epochs to converge, and the decay rate and batch size of mini-batch variants would otherwise need hyperparameter sweeps.
pt14gnV3dl.method: Applies an exponential moving average to mini-batch centroid updates using deep-learning machinery, and sets decay rate and batch size from fitted scaling laws. Reviews also mention a dead-cluster revival strategy.
pt14gnV3dl.key_idea: Mini-batch centroid updates use an exponential moving average whose decay rate and batch size follow fitted scaling laws, removing hyperparameter sweeps.
pt14gnV3dl.evidence: Scaling laws fit across problem sizes and embedding datasets, with comparisons to Lloyd k-means, k-means++ and Flash-KMeans on image and text embeddings, CPU and GPU, up to DINO10B.
pt14gnV3dl.claimed_gains: Beats Lloyd k-means loss at convergence in 1.2 to 3 epochs for a 10-45x GPU wall-clock speedup, and partitions 10 billion DINO embeddings into 16 million clusters in 2.5 epochs.
pt14gnV3dl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit faster convergence to lower error, a simple design that sets its own parameters, and a broad evaluation across embeddings, dataset sizes and CPU/GPU settings.
pt14gnV3dl.main_concern: It is unclear whether the gains come from the EMA strategy and scaling laws or from dead-cluster revival, and the scaling laws are fit mainly on a single dataset with little theory.

9kskCmPMqd.one_liner: Measures how FP8 and GPTQ quantization change batch-dependent answer flips under greedy LLM decoding and traces them to reduction order.
9kskCmPMqd.problem: Batching already makes greedy LLM inference non-deterministic, and it is unknown whether quantization changes this batch-context sensitivity.
9kskCmPMqd.method: Empirical study that holds prompts, decoding settings and checkpoints fixed while varying the serving context across BF16, GPTQ, FP8 weight-and-activation and FP8 KV-cache quantization, then tests batch-invariant kernels as an intervention.
9kskCmPMqd.key_idea: Batch composition changes the floating-point reduction order, and FP8 weight-and-activation quantization amplifies this order-dependent noise into more answer changes.
9kskCmPMqd.evidence: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on seven benchmarks and six serving contexts, smaller evaluations on five further models, and batch-invariant kernel tests.
9kskCmPMqd.claimed_gains: FP8 weight-and-activation quantization raises the answer-change rate from 8.7% to 17.2% for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and from 13.9% to 22.7% for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; batch-invariant kernels remove the effect for BF16 and FP8 at a throughput loss but not for GPTQ.
9kskCmPMqd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical relevance of reproducibility differences between quantization schemes and the controlled design, including batch-invariant tests and parse-failure treatments.
9kskCmPMqd.main_concern: The paper is mostly comparative measurement with limited mechanistic explanation of why FP8 amplifies variability, its mitigations are existing or inconclusive, and the GPTQ finding is generalized beyond what was tested.

OjDxyU2Td2.one_liner: Proves Adam-mini and Adam attain the minimax-optimal rate under heavy-tailed gradient noise, so noise alone cannot explain Muon's advantage.
OjDxyU2Td2.problem: Heavy-tailed gradient noise has been proposed to explain why Muon beats Adam, but it was unknown whether Adam can converge optimally under such noise.
OjDxyU2Td2.method: The paper analyzes Adam-mini, a blockwise framework covering Adam and Adam-Norm, under a bounded p-th noise moment, with support for bias correction and weight decay (hence AdamW). It adds a matching lower bound for stochastic l1 stationarity in smooth non-convex optimization.
OjDxyU2Td2.key_idea: Prove a sharp upper bound for blockwise Adam under heavy-tailed noise, matched by a minimax lower bound with unavoidable sqrt(d) dependence, then compare with Muon under the same problem class.
OjDxyU2Td2.evidence: Theory only: convergence upper and lower bounds; reviews note the absence of synthetic experiments verifying them.
OjDxyU2Td2.claimed_gains: Adam-mini attains the rate O(T^-(p-1)/(3p-2)) under heavy-tailed pth-moment noise, matched by a minimax lower bound with an unavoidable sqrt(d) dependence on the problem dimension d.
OjDxyU2Td2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory thorough and the optimal-rate result for AdamW and Adam-mini under heavy-tailed noise a strong contribution that covers practical features such as bias correction and weight decay.
OjDxyU2Td2.main_concern: The paper is very dense and hard to read (68 pages), and the stepsize and momentum choices depend on unknown quantities such as the optimality gap and noise level.

YNP2cX7hVN.one_liner: EgoMatrix turns monocular egocentric videos into bimanual dexterous robot trajectories and rendered observations via contact-aware reconstruction, retargeting and RL.
YNP2cX7hVN.problem: Converting egocentric human videos into reliable dexterous robot demonstrations requires accurate monocular hand-object reconstruction and physically consistent robot observations.
YNP2cX7hVN.method: EgoMatrix reconstructs manipulation-relevant geometry and contact, then uses retargeting and RL in simulation to produce successful trajectories, generates task-preserving augmented variants without repeating reconstruction or RL, and jointly renders robot hands and objects into matching observation videos.
YNP2cX7hVN.key_idea: Render robot hands and manipulated objects together from the same simulated RL rollout, so observations and actions stay geometrically consistent, after contact-aware hand-object reconstruction.
YNP2cX7hVN.evidence: Simulation on TACO, OakInk2 and self-collected data against baselines, reconstruction benchmarks on two public datasets, and real-robot tests fine-tuning pi0.5 on two bimanual tasks with 20 closed-loop trials per task.
YNP2cX7hVN.claimed_gains: 53.23% end-to-end success in simulation versus 14.52% for the strongest baseline, with the best reconstruction results on most metrics of two public benchmarks; the real-robot result is truncated in the abstract.
YNP2cX7hVN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the contact-aware multi-stage refinement and coherent end-to-end pipeline, noting that ablations show gains in trajectory-transfer success and that joint rendering preserves visual-action consistency.
YNP2cX7hVN.main_concern: Reviewers say the benefit of the generated data for downstream policy or VLA training is not directly validated, and the real-robot evaluation is limited and under-specified.

xWeKOH2FKS.one_liner: VIG-Sampler ranks tokens to unmask in diffusion multimodal LLMs by image-token attention and penalizes similar attention patterns.
xWeKOH2FKS.problem: Certainty-based token ordering in diffusion multimodal LLM decoding favors tokens frequent in training data, and influence-based ordering ignores the input image.
xWeKOH2FKS.method: VIG-Sampler prioritizes candidate tokens by their attention to image tokens and adds a constraint that penalizes candidates whose image-attention distributions resemble those of already selected tokens, increasing the information gain of the decoded subset.
xWeKOH2FKS.key_idea: Score masked positions by attention mass on image tokens and subtract a similarity penalty against previously selected tokens' image-attention distributions, using attention from the same forward pass.
xWeKOH2FKS.evidence: 7 captioning and VQA benchmarks with 3 open-source diffusion multimodal LLMs, compared with the Info-Gain Sampler and confidence-based samplers across decoding budgets and generation lengths.
xWeKOH2FKS.claimed_gains: Outperforms the Info-Gain Sampler by an average of 19.3 CIDEr points across the captioning benchmarks and surpasses it on COCO Caption using only half as many decoding steps.
xWeKOH2FKS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the sampler training-free and lightweight (no extra forward passes) and the evaluation comprehensive across models, decoding budgets, generation lengths and hyperparameters.
xWeKOH2FKS.main_concern: Attention to image tokens is an unverified proxy for correct or informative predictions, and penalizing attention similarity may delay useful attribute or relation tokens; evaluation is limited to captioning and simple VQA.

jQagboByhg.one_liner: SpeakingRobot schedules word-level semantic gesture events with an LLM and refines retrieved robot-space priors with heterogeneous whole-body diffusion.
jQagboByhg.problem: Humanoid co-speech gestures are injected either as soft conditions that drift from their word or as hard constraints that copy retrieved clips with dynamics the robot cannot execute.
jQagboByhg.method: A language model schedules sparse word-level semantic events and a robot-space prior is retrieved for each. A heterogeneous whole-body diffusion initializes only the scheduled upper-body regions from lightly corrupted priors and the rest (torso, pelvis, legs) from Gaussian noise, and one denoiser refines them jointly; training with cross-instance priors rewards adapting a prior rather than copying it.
jQagboByhg.key_idea: Treat retrieved gestures as editable priors: fix which action occurs at which word, but start upper-body regions from lightly noised priors and everything else from pure noise.
jQagboByhg.evidence: Experiments on two benchmarks and a real-robot user study, with tracking success measured using a fixed GMT tracker and a hard-anchor baseline comparison.
jQagboByhg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper delivers semantic co-speech gestures on a humanoid robot with coordinated whole-body execution, and find the execution-success results with a fixed GMT tracker the strongest evidence.
jQagboByhg.main_concern: The contribution beyond existing motion-prior methods (LivelySpeaker, RAG-Gesture) is not isolated by ablations, and details such as gesture vocabulary selection, noise level, and the LLM scheduler's contribution are under-specified.

1nK74FrfKK.one_liner: Brief weight-decay perturbations across the pre-generalization plateau reveal a stable dose-ordered shift in grokking time.
1nK74FrfKK.problem: It is unclear how solution selection develops during the long plateau between fitting the training data and visible generalization in grokking.
1nK74FrfKK.method: They sweep short fixed-duration weight decay perturbations across the plateau, measure shifts in later generalization time, and compute test-loss barriers between perturbed and baseline checkpoints. They name the resulting pattern canalization of grokking solution selection.
1nK74FrfKK.key_idea: Apply short fixed-duration weight-decay perturbations at different plateau times and measure generalization-time shifts and loss barriers to probe regularization-driven dynamics.
1nK74FrfKK.evidence: Three grokking tasks with weight-decay dose sweeps and loss-barrier measurements, plus a similar response under l1 regularization in the setting of Tikeng Notsawo et al. (2025).
1nK74FrfKK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the intervention design is clean and carefully controlled, and that the ordered timing response late in the plateau is an interesting probe of a hidden pre-generalization transition.
1nK74FrfKK.main_concern: The mechanism is unresolved and the scope is narrow: three small algorithmic tasks with clean plateaus, with unclear generalization to other architectures or settings without a plateau.

a71eA6z2Zh.one_liner: Distills an 8-step image generator into a 2-step model using teacher-generated GAN targets and step-specific parameters.
a71eA6z2Zh.problem: Few-step distillation is mature for 4-8 steps, but 2-step generation is limited by task difficulty and model capacity.
a71eA6z2Zh.method: Z-Image Ultra-Turbo is distilled from the 8-step Z-Image Turbo teacher with teacher-image adversarial training, separate parameters per denoising step, and end-to-end training with an explicit step-1 loss.
a71eA6z2Zh.key_idea: Use teacher-generated images as GAN real samples, give each of the two steps its own parameters, and train end-to-end with a step-1 regularization loss.
a71eA6z2Zh.evidence: Qualitative and quantitative comparisons with the 8-step teacher and 2-step baselines; reviews cite LongText-CN/EN and OneIG scores and ablations.
a71eA6z2Zh.claimed_gains: Substantially narrows the quality gap between 2-step and 8-step generation; the abstract gives no numbers.
a71eA6z2Zh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the 2-step model comes close to the 8-step teacher and beats public 2-step baselines, notably on text rendering.
a71eA6z2Zh.main_concern: Each design has uncited precedents (e.g., LADD for teacher-generated adversarial data, Phased DMD for step-wise experts), which weakens the novelty claim.

1VPvaYoLeK.one_liner: Proves how the number of separately risk-controlled severe error groups changes the information a representation must retain.
1VPvaYoLeK.problem: When errors have unequal consequences, finer separate risk limits may demand more information from a finite-message representation, and this cost is not characterized.
1VPvaYoLeK.method: The paper studies finite-message representations fixed before risk budgets are set, defines frontier error, and proves rates for grouping the same severe error events into m groups, with checks on synthetic data and WiCE.
1VPvaYoLeK.key_idea: Hold the source and error events fixed while splitting severe errors into m separately limited groups, and show the optimal M-message frontier error rate changes with m.
1VPvaYoLeK.evidence: Theorems for a regular class of classification problems with a common default and one competing action; synthetic experiments; frozen, calibrated WiCE verifier outputs.
1VPvaYoLeK.claimed_gains: Optimal M-message frontier error is Theta(M^(-2/m)) for m groups; empirical effects are illustrated without numbers in the abstract.
1VPvaYoLeK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the main theoretical comparison is clear and crisp, and that synthetic experiments align with the theory.
1VPvaYoLeK.main_concern: The WiCE experiment gives limited evidence about real risk control, and the theory covers a specialized setting with one default and one competing action.

iGQaftL7Xp.one_liner: Model-free Umbrella RL using a DualDICE-style density-ratio estimator and a saddle-point critic to maximize return plus state-distribution entropy.
iGQaftL7Xp.problem: Hard RL problems combine sparse reward, state traps and no terminal state, and the original Umbrella RL needs analytical dynamics and their divergence in continuous time.
iGQaftL7Xp.method: MF URL is a discrete-time instantiation trained from independent one-step queries to a resettable simulator. It adapts DualDICE with a known proposal density as the ratio denominator to obtain the discounted state occupancy density, and trains a critic with separate value and advantage heads through a second saddle-point objective.
iGQaftL7Xp.key_idea: Estimate discounted state occupancy via a DualDICE density ratio against a known proposal density, then optimize return plus occupancy entropy with a saddle-point critic.
iGQaftL7Xp.evidence: Multi-Valley Mountain Car and StandUp, compared with Model Based URL, SAC and PPO.
iGQaftL7Xp.claimed_gains: MF URL policies reach and remain in the reward regions with returns comparable to Model Based URL; no numbers stated.
iGQaftL7Xp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that removing the need for analytical dynamics is a mathematically grounded extension of Umbrella RL.
iGQaftL7Xp.main_concern: Sample efficiency is poor and the method is complex (many simulator queries, resets to arbitrary states), with simple evaluation tasks, limited originality and a missing fair baseline with the same simulator access.

2YImymyWbx.one_liner: Tracks Gram matrices of latent representations to decompose learning-time motion into growth, spectral allocation, rotation, and transport for early warning.
2YImymyWbx.problem: A model can reorganize internally before a new capability shows in its outputs, so intervention may require expensive rollbacks unless such changes are detected early and cheaply.
2YImymyWbx.method: Builds Gram matrices from latent representations on relevant inputs and gives an invariant decomposition of motion into growth, spectral allocation, internal rotation, and support transport, then derives scalar early-warning signals.
2YImymyWbx.key_idea: Normalized representation geometry can move before amplitude-dependent measures reveal an emerging response, because response amplitude is tied to the rate of its geometric motion.
2YImymyWbx.evidence: Three settings with decreasing prior knowledge of future learning events: deep linear networks, induction heads, and the Pythia suite.
2YImymyWbx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important and the framework principled, with a clear theoretical explanation of why internal learning can precede behavior and a careful past-only alarm design.
2YImymyWbx.main_concern: Empirical validation is thin: the induction and Pythia experiments are largely qualitative, without baselines, false-positive rates, or threshold sensitivity, and the blind alarm may track existing structure.

Ly6TUFXbuy.one_liner: Builds teacher-written traces from behavioral prototypes and selected history events to adapt pretrained generative recommenders to new verticals.
Ly6TUFXbuy.problem: Continual pretraining and fine-tuning on individual histories leave recurring domain behavior patterns, and a user's position within a pattern, implicit when target-domain data are scarce.
Ly6TUFXbuy.method: ProtoAdapter builds a prototype bank from the target-domain corpus, retrieves compatible prototypes per history, selects supporting events, and has a teacher write a structured trace (pattern, evidence, transition bridge) ending in the target action; trace and direct-answer examples are mixed for training while deployment keeps direct item-token generation.
Ly6TUFXbuy.key_idea: Make domain-level behavioral prototypes and history-specific evidence explicit as teacher-written traces used as training supervision, while inference still generates item tokens directly.
Ly6TUFXbuy.evidence: Several recommendation datasets (including KuaiRand) with Qwen3 and OneRec backbones, three datasets and three ranking metrics per the reviews, plus low-data settings and ablations.
Ly6TUFXbuy.claimed_gains: Consistent improvements across ranking metrics, more pronounced in low-data settings; the KuaiRand figure is cut off in the abstract.
Ly6TUFXbuy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining domain-wide behavior prototypes with history-specific evidence is a well-motivated approach that improves two backbones on all three datasets, especially with little data.
Ly6TUFXbuy.main_concern: Possible label leakage: evidence selection and teacher traces use the target item, and the ablations do not separate prototype retrieval from target-aware rationale supervision.

m4279bKxM2.one_liner: Mean-field theory predicts per-class accuracy from within-class variability aligned with true and rival class centroids across vision, audio and language.
m4279bKxM2.problem: It is hard to identify which geometric features of high-dimensional neural representations determine predictive performance.
m4279bKxM2.method: They identify within-class variability aligned with the class centroid and competing centroids, derive an analytical mean-field theory from projections along true-class and rival-class centroid directions with a global class-radius renormalization, and test it across models in vision, audio and language.
m4279bKxM2.key_idea: Within-class variability is aligned with the class's own and rival centroids, so accuracy follows from projection statistics on a few centroid directions plus a radius renormalization.
m4279bKxM2.evidence: Per-class accuracy predictions across tasks, architectures and modalities (36 models per a reviewer), with random-rotation interventions on within-class residuals.
m4279bKxM2.claimed_gains: The theory accurately predicts per-class accuracy across tasks, architectures and modalities; no numeric figures are stated in the abstract.
m4279bKxM2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a shared geometric structure across models and modalities, with an analytical theory that matches empirical per-class accuracy and explains scale effects.
m4279bKxM2.main_concern: The causal reading of the rotation experiment is stronger than the evidence, since randomly rotating residuals in high dimensions removes centroid-aligned components by construction; dense writing and unreleased code were also raised.

Tsqun8N1mn.one_liner: Few-shot class-incremental learning with frozen backbones using prior-guided distribution calibration and recursive class-balanced analytic prototype updates in kernel space.
Tsqun8N1mn.problem: Frozen pre-trained backbones adapt insufficiently to novel concepts, few-shot prototypes are statistically biased, and static prototypes lack global discriminative optimization.
Tsqun8N1mn.method: Prior-Guided Distribution Calibration uses base-class priors to improve representation discriminability, and a Global Knowledge-Aware Solver recursively updates class-balanced weights in a shared kernel space without revisiting historical images, with a theoretical argument that it mitigates catastrophic forgetting.
Tsqun8N1mn.key_idea: Calibrate few-shot class distributions with base-class priors, then solve class-balanced analytic classifier weights recursively in an RBF kernel space as new classes arrive.
Tsqun8N1mn.evidence: CIFAR-100, CUB-200 and ImageNet-R with ResNet-18, ViT-B-IN21K and CLIP-ViT-B backbones, component ablations, a time and memory comparison, and add-on tests with SEC-Prompt and CASP.
Tsqun8N1mn.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically in the visible abstract, which reports consistent improvements over representative feature- and classifier-level methods.
Tsqun8N1mn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree DAP gives the best average accuracy across the evaluated dataset-backbone settings, with clear time and memory benefits from recursive updates and no backbone optimization.
Tsqun8N1mn.main_concern: Novelty over prior calibration and analytic-learning work (Goswami et al., GKEAL) is unclear, and the theoretical claims on separability and diagonal dominance are not supported by the stated inequalities.

UsuubceSRw.one_liner: Training-free peptide binder design combining go-explore-style binding-basin exploration with physics-guided local refinement for linear and cyclic peptides.
UsuubceSRw.problem: Training-free peptide design methods reuse pretrained structure predictors but explore diverse binding poses inefficiently on difficult targets, and peptide structure prediction and scoring are insufficiently benchmarked.
UsuubceSRw.method: A two-stage framework: global proposal uses state replay, dynamic structural cell partitioning and revisit penalties to explore binding basins systematically, then local refinement optimizes interfaces within selected basins using physics-based scoring. It extends to multi-target binders and macrocyclic molecular glues.
UsuubceSRw.key_idea: Archive-based exploration of binding basins (state replay, structural-cell partitioning, revisit penalties) over a pretrained co-folding model, followed by physics-scored local interface refinement.
UsuubceSRw.evidence: Structural and binding benchmarks of predictors and scores, then comparisons against five external baselines over multiple targets and peptide topologies, with orthogonal prediction, steric and energetic checks.
UsuubceSRw.claimed_gains: Substantially outperforms five external baselines in throughput of in silico-accepted pose clusters, particularly on challenging targets and cyclic topologies, with gains sustained under orthogonal checks (no numbers stated).
UsuubceSRw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is comprehensive and practical, covering multiple targets and topologies with useful predictor and scoring benchmarks.
UsuubceSRw.main_concern: Success depends on the same co-folding confidence model used for generation and the advantage shrinks under an orthogonal evaluator, suggesting evaluator exploitation, while ablations use single seeds.

BlMyc5iZzn.one_liner: Minimal audio watermarking using bounded magnitude scaling for imperceptibility and a lightweight readout head on low-level audio representations for robustness.
BlMyc5iZzn.problem: Multi-bit audio watermarks are vulnerable to neural codec resynthesis and voice cloning, and existing methods stack attack simulation, latent watermarking and perceptual losses whose necessity is unclear.
BlMyc5iZzn.method: SimpleMark embeds the watermark through bounded magnitude scaling and detects it from low-level audio representations with a lightweight readout head, yielding a series of lightweight watermarking models.
BlMyc5iZzn.key_idea: Scale the signal's magnitude within a bound to embed, and read the watermark linearly from low-level representations, without attack simulation, latent embedding or perceptual losses.
BlMyc5iZzn.evidence: A subtractive study of prior strategies and evaluation against traditional editing attacks, 30 neural codecs and voice cloning systems (per reviews), with MOS and PESQ quality measures.
BlMyc5iZzn.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically; it claims robustness competitive with existing methods without complex architectures or training strategies, and a superior robustness-imperceptibility trade-off.
BlMyc5iZzn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it shows codec- and cloning-robust watermarking does not require attack simulation, latent embedding or perceptual losses, using a simple, interpretable architecture.
BlMyc5iZzn.main_concern: Imperceptibility is weaker than claimed (MOS 3.78, PESQ trailing several baselines), and the learned watermark is a fixed content-agnostic frequency pattern with no adaptive-attack evaluation.

trtvXobU44.one_liner: Reuses historical self-generated rollouts for offline SFT, keeping the full trajectory as context but applying loss only to selected continuations.
trtvXobU44.problem: Rollouts from RL and on-policy distillation are treated as stale once the policy advances, though they can preserve behaviors the policy no longer expresses reliably, alongside mistakes and redundant actions not worth imitating.
trtvXobU44.method: ROSS preserves the whole historical trajectory as context and applies loss only to selected model-generated continuations, with selection done by an external reviewer model (GLM-5.2 per reviews), training through offline SFT with no additional policy rollouts.
trtvXobU44.key_idea: Mask the SFT loss to reviewer-selected segments of past rollouts while keeping the rest of the trajectory in context.
trtvXobU44.evidence: Domain-specific RL, multi-teacher on-policy distillation and agentic RL on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, across mathematics, code generation, instruction following and software engineering.
trtvXobU44.claimed_gains: On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, ROSS improves the six-benchmark MOPD average from 58.40% to 62.20% and SWE-bench Verified from 64.20% to 68.40%.
trtvXobU44.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically motivated and the approach is cheap to adopt, with broad verification across RL and distillation runs and an informative filtering-versus-masking ablation.
trtvXobU44.main_concern: Gains may come from a strong external model choosing the supervised tokens (implicit distillation), the value of historical rollouts is not isolated from equally curated fresh data, and results are single-run.

QOzEeBE50D.one_liner: Hypernetwork-free meta model editor using the raw gradient plus a direct residual and history-aware regularization, with two scalars per layer.
QOzEeBE50D.problem: Meta-learning model editors transform the first-step edit gradient with a learned hypernetwork, but it is unclear how much that transformation contributes to sequential editing.
QOzEeBE50D.method: RawEdit directly uses the raw first-step gradient and strengthens the update with a direct residual and history-aware regularization that accounts for previously edited directions; it learns only two scalars per edited layer to control edit strength and regularization.
QOzEeBE50D.key_idea: Drop the learned gradient transformation and build the update from the raw gradient with residual fitting and a regularizer against previously edited directions.
QOzEeBE50D.evidence: Analyses across multiple meta editors, language models and datasets showing untransformed updates are competitive, then long-horizon sequential editing with up to 20,000 edits.
QOzEeBE50D.claimed_gains: Outperforms existing editors by up to 20% in efficacy, generality and locality while substantially reducing computational cost, and stays stable under up to 20,000 sequential edits.
QOzEeBE50D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question of whether hypernetworks are needed is important and the component analysis is systematic and informative beyond introducing another editor.
QOzEeBE50D.main_concern: Methodological novelty is seen as incremental relative to MEMIT/AlphaEdit-style and RLEdit formulations, and the efficacy metrics use teacher-forced evaluation that may overestimate editing performance.

Tnhg2WskM6.one_liner: LLM unlearning that analytically edits to forget, then projects non-target outputs back toward the original model under fixed forgetting constraints.
Tnhg2WskM6.problem: Unlearning that reaches the desired forgetting level leaves collateral changes that impair non-target behavior, and some of these can be reversed without losing the forgetting.
Tnhg2WskM6.method: PTP-U first applies local analytic edits to weaken target knowledge associations, then aligns non-target output distributions with the original model to recover capabilities while holding the forgetting constraints fixed.
Tnhg2WskM6.key_idea: Propose a local analytic forgetting edit, then project the model to match original non-target output distributions subject to fixed forgetting constraints.
Tnhg2WskM6.evidence: Three primary benchmarks, several model families and eight baselines (per reviews), with recovery comparisons and ablation studies.
Tnhg2WskM6.claimed_gains: PTP-U reaches 81.22%–91.03% forgetting while preserving 94.20% non-target utility on average, and at matched forgetting retains higher non-target utility.
Tnhg2WskM6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the recoverable-drift motivation is clear and the two-stage design is principled, with broad experiments across models and tasks.
Tnhg2WskM6.main_concern: Results depend on a hand-chosen layer (around layer 23) that may not transfer across model scales, with single-run tables and a heavy, partly under-specified pipeline.

SfYmNLzBGl.one_liner: One-shot pre-indexing corpus attack on neural subgraph retrievers: greedy set-function maximization over perturbed corpus graphs, accelerated by ANN-based pruning.
SfYmNLzBGl.problem: A third-party vendor with read/write corpus access could corrupt graphs before indexing, degrading future queries of a neural subgraph retriever.
SfYmNLzBGl.method: QUPAC perturbs a small subset of corpus graphs once with label-preserving node-pair perturbations, formulated as cardinality-constrained set-function maximization of a ranking loss solved greedily. It prunes the candidate ground set with approximate nearest neighbor search on a query-specific attack score approximating marginal gain.
SfYmNLzBGl.key_idea: Cast the attack as cardinality-constrained set-function maximization and replace the exhaustive greedy scan with ANN lookup on an inner-product form of an approximate marginal gain.
SfYmNLzBGl.evidence: Multiple datasets and NSR architectures (IsoNet, IsoNet++, GMN) under white-box, black-box and transfer regimes, against adapted baselines, plus a greedy approximation guarantee.
SfYmNLzBGl.claimed_gains: Not stated in the visible abstract.
SfYmNLzBGl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pre-indexing universal-poisoning setting is practically relevant and the formulation is clean, with consistent gains over adapted baselines across datasets and threat regimes.
SfYmNLzBGl.main_concern: The attack effect is modest given the adversary's power (about a 17 percent drop in mean average precision), and scalability is not tested beyond small molecular graph corpora.

CdD3BBoTA4.one_liner: Regularizes INR training with learned nonlocal patch relations via a wavelet-domain graph-residual regularizer for missing-region completion.
CdD3BBoTA4.problem: INRs are supervised only at observed locations, and local smoothness priors blur the interior of large missing regions because they cannot borrow edges and textures from similar structures elsewhere in the image.
CdD3BBoTA4.method: LNRR learns patch relations with a patch feature network and uses them to constrain the reconstruction of missing regions through a robust graph-residual regularizer in the wavelet domain. It changes only the regularization term, so it applies to many INR backbones and other representations.
CdD3BBoTA4.key_idea: Learn within-image patch affinities with a feature network and penalize graph residuals of the reconstruction in the wavelet domain, as a backbone-agnostic regularizer.
CdD3BBoTA4.evidence: Multiple natural-image datasets and missing patterns, with INR backbones plus Deep Image Prior and 2D Gaussian representations, and ablations.
CdD3BBoTA4.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically; the abstract reports the best completion among existing INR regularization methods and improvements for Deep Image Prior and 2D Gaussian representations.
CdD3BBoTA4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the regularizer is well motivated, simple and backbone agnostic, with consistent improvements over prior work in quantitative and qualitative results.
CdD3BBoTA4.main_concern: Experiments are limited (few 256x256 images, only inpainting, no standard deviations or significance tests), and dense sections on the robust potential are hard to follow.

Wsclgm9qCc.one_liner: Weisfeiler-Leman message passing for graphs embedded on surfaces, using rotation systems, with a proved expressivity hierarchy and a topological GNN.
Wsclgm9qCc.problem: Connectivity alone is often insufficient for chemically meaningful predictions while full 3D structure is not needed and can hinder learning, and existing topological deep learning ignores the topology of embeddings.
Wsclgm9qCc.method: Three methods exploit the embedding via its induced rotation system: sparse cyclic aggregations, dense aggregations with a ternary relation on vertices, and dense aggregations with binary relations on oriented edges. The authors prove their expressivity and propose GNNs evaluated on topological property prediction and chirality-sensitive molecular tasks.
Wsclgm9qCc.key_idea: Aggregate over the cyclic order of neighbours given by a surface embedding's rotation system, with ternary vertex or binary dart relations for completeness.
Wsclgm9qCc.evidence: Proofs of expressivity for each aggregation scheme, plus experiments on topological property prediction and chirality-sensitive molecular tasks (and MANTRA per reviews).
Wsclgm9qCc.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically; the theoretical results are that sparse cyclic aggregations identify all embedded trees, ternary dense aggregations identify all embedded graphs at dimension three and not below, and binary edge relations do so already at dimension two.
Wsclgm9qCc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the exact WL completeness bounds and expressivity comparisons are the main strength, and the synthetic experiments follow the theory.
Wsclgm9qCc.main_concern: The complete tests are never implemented as trained models (the GNN covers only the weaker 2-TWL rotation refinement), experiments use very small graphs, and MANTRA includes non-orientable surfaces outside the theory.

SlhSJVDBjB.one_liner: Benchmark for navigating from underspecified everyday requests, with matched-trajectory language conditions, plus HiNav closed-loop textual guidance for VLN executors.
SlhSJVDBjB.problem: Vision-language navigation benchmarks cover route instructions and goals but not underspecified everyday requests that need target grounding, spatial reasoning and route planning from incomplete navigation information.
SlhSJVDBjB.method: RG-VLN pairs each trajectory with detailed route instructions, route-preserving paraphrases and underspecified requests with progressively less route information, over 6,000 episodes across MP3D and HM3D with VLM-generated and human-written requests. HiNav provides closed-loop textual guidance to plug-and-play VLN executors.
SlhSJVDBjB.key_idea: Hold trajectories fixed while varying language specificity to isolate navigation-detail loss, and guide executors with closed-loop textual feedback (HiNav).
SlhSJVDBjB.evidence: Over 6,000 episodes on MP3D and HM3D scenes evaluating representative VLN methods under three language conditions, with HiNav compared against baselines.
SlhSJVDBjB.claimed_gains: Replacing detailed instructions with underspecified requests reduces the success rates of representative VLN methods by 68.5%–74.2%, whereas route-preserving paraphrases cause only minor changes.
SlhSJVDBjB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the matched-trajectory design cleanly attributes the success-rate collapse to reduced navigation specification rather than wording, and that the benchmark fills a realistic gap.
SlhSJVDBjB.main_concern: HiNav is fine-tuned on synthesized episodes while baselines use official weights, so margins mix method and adaptation budget, and benchmark solvability and VLM-generator bias are not independently validated.

36IAuaaGIZ.one_liner: Bitwise-exact, batch-invariant test-time query optimization for late-interaction retrieval using tensor-core filtering, certified working sets, and a fixed-order fused loop.
36IAuaaGIZ.problem: In late-interaction test-time query optimization, TF32 tensor cores and batch-dependent library matrix products change maxima and bits, so the same request can return different rankings under different batching or kernels.
36IAuaaGIZ.method: ExactTTO makes TTO runs bitwise identical to a fixed-order FP32 reference: tensor cores only filter candidates whose FP32 maxima are then recomputed exactly, certified working sets skip rescans that cannot change the result, and a fused loop applies each step's gradient and Adam update in a fixed order.
36IAuaaGIZ.key_idea: Let approximate tensor-core computation choose which products to compute, but recompute selected values in fixed-order FP32 and certify skipped rescans so results stay exact.
36IAuaaGIZ.evidence: Protocols of GQR and ReFIT on ViDoRe and BEIR, tested under multiple batchings, with comparisons to GQR's FP32 scorer, a batch-invariant FP32 matrix product and FLASH-MaxSim.
36IAuaaGIZ.claimed_gains: In batches of 64 requests, ExactTTO serves 5.93× as many queries per second as GQR's FP32 scorer, 4.76× as many as a tuned batch-invariant FP32 matrix product and 1.29× as many as FLASH-MaxSim's inexact TF32 path, while every query keeps its reference ranking under every batching tested.
36IAuaaGIZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the exactness argument is technically rigorous and validated by lockstep audits, and that batch invariance in retrieval-time optimization is a relevant, underexplored problem.
36IAuaaGIZ.main_concern: The practical value of bitwise exactness is not demonstrated, since the measured ranking and nDCG changes are small, and the speedups rest on narrow baselines and are lost at batch size 1.

w9tVu9p4x3.one_liner: Molecule-text retrieval with query-conditioned multiple molecular tokens, trained on a synthetic caption dataset generated from structured molecular information.
w9tVu9p4x3.problem: Existing molecule-text datasets use database or literature descriptions of variable content that do not consistently emphasize properties derivable from molecular structure.
w9tVu9p4x3.method: MolSynText is a synthetic dataset whose descriptions are generated from structured molecular information and screened for consistency with their source. MolTokSyn represents each molecule with multiple learned tokens and uses the text query to decide how the tokens are combined for scoring.
w9tVu9p4x3.key_idea: Represent a molecule by several learned tokens combined with query-dependent weights, so different descriptions emphasize different molecular aspects.
w9tVu9p4x3.evidence: Bidirectional molecule-text retrieval on MolSynText and PubChem-derived text, property-prediction transfer, and a Controlled Semantic Benchmark of structural, physicochemical and relational properties.
w9tVu9p4x3.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically; the abstract reports consistent gains over strong existing methods on MolSynText, competitive results on matched PubChem-derived text, and strong transfer to property prediction.
w9tVu9p4x3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the chemically grounded synthetic supervision is useful, the setup is well controlled across architectures and splits, and the gains are broad.
w9tVu9p4x3.main_concern: Ablations do not show that query conditioning drives the gains (a single-token variant performs about as well), and synthetic text quality is checked only by the LLM that generated it.

CTOWnmnRI1.one_liner: Training-free model merging that selects task subspaces and defines cross-task orthogonality using a data-induced metric estimated from unlabeled samples.
CTOWnmnRI1.problem: Spectral merging orthogonalizes directions in Euclidean weight space, but directions orthogonal in parameters can still overlap in the activations the model actually sees.
CTOWnmnRI1.method: It derives a joint least-squares view that unifies several merging methods, then replaces Euclidean geometry with a data-induced metric from a few unlabeled samples to choose each task's low-rank subspace and define cross-task orthogonality, preserving the expert update within the chosen subspace.
CTOWnmnRI1.key_idea: Orthogonalize task-vector subspaces under the activation-covariance metric (square-root weighting) instead of the Euclidean metric.
CTOWnmnRI1.evidence: Vision, GLUE and generative merging benchmarks, with validation sweeps of the metric weighting and ablations separating data-aware subspace selection from data-aware orthogonalization.
CTOWnmnRI1.claimed_gains: F-TSV consistently improves over its Euclidean counterpart across all reported benchmarks, with data-aware cross-task orthogonalization accounting for almost all of the gains in vision (no numbers stated).
CTOWnmnRI1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the change of orthogonality criterion is clearly motivated and the paper is well organized, with theory and ablations that separate subspace selection from orthogonalization.
CTOWnmnRI1.main_concern: Overlap with existing data-aware spectral merging methods (PAVE, ESM) is not cleanly resolved, and data-aware subspace selection adds little outside GLUE.

cgkxaQZ2Hb.one_liner: Two-stage RL framework training one policy to acquire, apply and revise executable tool skills without supervised skill-operation labels.
cgkxaQZ2Hb.problem: Existing tool-skill approaches rely on fragmented skill learning, skill-operation supervision or natural-language skill representations rather than jointly managing executable skills.
cgkxaQZ2Hb.method: Stage one uses a progressive curriculum from reference-guided skill construction to autonomous skill acquisition and refinement. Stage two uses a leave-one-scenario-out strategy to train the policy to retain, revise or rebuild imperfectly matched transferred skills across task interactions.
cgkxaQZ2Hb.key_idea: A curriculum that fades reference guidance, then leave-one-scenario-out RL so the policy learns to keep, revise or rebuild transferred executable skills without supervised skill operations.
cgkxaQZ2Hb.evidence: AppWorld under independent transfer, sequential adaptation and cold-start acquisition, plus BFCL-v3 generalization, mostly with a 4B model (per reviews).
cgkxaQZ2Hb.claimed_gains: On AppWorld, A3-Skill improves TGC over the strongest baseline by 13.63% under sequential adaptation and 15.78% under cold-start acquisition, and reaches 32.00% accuracy on BFCL-v3 versus 28.00% for the strongest baseline.
cgkxaQZ2Hb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated, the two-stage design is coherent, and the analyses of executable versus textual skills and skill-management decisions are informative.
cgkxaQZ2Hb.main_concern: The contribution is incremental over closely related RL-trained executable-skill work such as SAGE, absolute gains are small, and baseline training budgets are underspecified with tests on one 4B model.

jpLJRwjrpk.one_liner: Matching complexity bounds for stochastic first-order optimization with almost-surely bounded gradient noise across nonconvex, PL, strongly convex and convex objectives.
jpLJRwjrpk.problem: It is unclear whether bounded-variance complexity rates change when gradient noise has a prescribed almost-sure norm bound, especially when algorithms may reuse samples and query them adaptively.
jpLJRwjrpk.method: It proves matching bounds for randomized algorithms that retain samples, query them adaptively and observe exact function values, distinguishing smoothness of the objective from smoothness of the centered noise and identifying the benefit of evaluating one sample at several points. Lower bounds use scalar sample losses with bounded noise on the whole domain.
jpLJRwjrpk.key_idea: Encode each unknown direction with a continuous bounded distribution (Poisson-kernel observations) and control adaptive information to extend single-query bounded-noise lower bounds to finite batches.
jpLJRwjrpk.evidence: Theoretical lower and matching upper bounds for four objective classes and finite sums; reviews note there is no empirical evidence for the modeling assumption.
jpLJRwjrpk.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically; the abstract reports matching complexity bounds for smooth nonconvex, Polyak-Lojasiewicz, strongly convex and convex objectives.
jpLJRwjrpk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the lower bounds are a strong, fairly complete treatment that holds for randomized, adaptive algorithms and shows the bounded-variance barrier persists under almost-sure bounded noise.
jpLJRwjrpk.main_concern: The practical motivation for uniformly bounded gradient noise is unconvincing and lacks empirical support, and the dimension-growth lower-bound construction leaves fixed-dimension parallel-query gains unresolved.

9NcLBhJett.one_liner: Rank fusion cast as a restricted-support Wasserstein barycenter, solved by greedy submodular maximization with ANN-based marginal-gain approximation.
9NcLBhJett.problem: Pointwise fusion of lexical, sparse and dense rankers ignores relationships among retrieved documents in embedding space, treating near-duplicate clusters and complementary subsets alike.
9NcLBhJett.method: It recasts fusion as a Restricted Support Wasserstein Barycenter problem that jointly optimizes the retrieved set and its ranking, then as a monotone, restricted-submodular set function maximized greedily. Each greedy marginal-gain step is approximated with an ANN index (DiskANN, Faiss) to avoid corpus-wide search.
9NcLBhJett.key_idea: Select the fused result set by greedy maximization of a barycenter-based submodular objective, turning each marginal-gain step into an approximate maximum-inner-product search.
9NcLBhJett.evidence: Experiments on five datasets with ablations, comparing ranking accuracy, corpus geometry and query latency, plus approximation guarantees for the greedy solver.
9NcLBhJett.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically; the abstract reports favorable trade-offs among ranking accuracy, corpus geometry and query latency.
9NcLBhJett.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the set-level barycenter view of fusion is a reasonable, timely idea with comprehensive proofs and solid experiments including ablations.
9NcLBhJett.main_concern: It is unclear how much of the accuracy gain comes from the barycenter rather than the reranker (the same reranker without the barycenter target nearly matches it), and the guarantees do not cover the implemented ANN pipeline.

dn6zk6OOOE.one_liner: Unbiased semi-value estimator with size-wise mean and linear control variates fit on past batches, at linear cost.
dn6zk6OOOE.problem: Adalina's single global scalar control variate cannot capture variation among same-size coalitions, and fitting it on the samples it corrects induces an O(1/T) bias.
dn6zk6OOOE.method: SLICE adds a size-wise mean and a size-wise linear control variate with closed-form centering, both fit only on past batches and held fixed for the current one, keeping unbiasedness at finite sample size, linear cost and log n-free query complexity.
dn6zk6OOOE.key_idea: Fit coalition-size-specific mean and linear control variates on earlier batches only, so the current batch's correction stays predictable and unbiased.
dn6zk6OOOE.evidence: 14 utilities compared with O(n)-memory estimators and regression-adjusted estimators that store coalitions, including a 16 GB memory setting, plus theory on unbiasedness and non-increased MSE with population-optimal coefficients.
dn6zk6OOOE.claimed_gains: SLICE attains the lowest error among the tested O(n)-memory estimators in most settings at moderate-to-large budgets, with typical crossover budgets of a few tens of queries per player.
dn6zk6OOOE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SLICE is a simple, effective improvement over Adalina with sound unbiasedness and complexity analysis and encouraging empirical results.
dn6zk6OOOE.main_concern: The experimental scope is narrow, with closely related baselines missing (Linear MSR, Tree MSR), only tree-ensemble utilities, and little analysis of hyperparameters and the warm-up and gating strategies.

mCiMdbopCG.one_liner: Federated LoRA that initializes shared adapters from population gradients and picks frozen private spectral bases from client residual gradients.
mCiMdbopCG.problem: Factor similarity is used to decide what to share in federated LoRA, but similar factors may reflect common initialization and server history, and a single gradient step can give aligned factors with opposite effective updates.
mCiMdbopCG.method: GReP-LoRA initializes a shared adapter from the population gradient and selects frozen private spectral bases from client residual gradients. Clients learn shared tangent increments and compact private cores that rescale and combine the selected directions, and only shared parameters are aggregated.
mCiMdbopCG.key_idea: Use task gradients rather than factor similarity to define shared and private LoRA subspaces, aggregating only the shared component.
mCiMdbopCG.evidence: Vision and language tasks (DomainNet and NICO++ per reviews) with held-out gradient prediction, private-branch transfer experiments, controlled comparisons, and theory under quadratic assumptions with nonconvex stationarity bounds.
mCiMdbopCG.claimed_gains: Not stated in the visible abstract.
mCiMdbopCG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the finding that similar LoRA factors need not imply aligned update directions is a valuable new perspective on selective sharing.
mCiMdbopCG.main_concern: Private spectral bases are chosen once from starting gradients and frozen, with limited validation that this selection is needed and weaker results than FedSA-LoRA on some domains.

aI4Dxf0xSG.one_liner: Exact finite-sample certify-or-abstain audits of thresholded-decision operating rates under r-wise independence, solved as discrete moment problems with primal-dual certificates.
aI4Dxf0xSG.problem: Operating-rate claims for thresholded decisions are usually assessed under independence, although evaluation units may share a patient, time series or prompt.
aI4Dxf0xSG.method: Under r-wise independence, symmetrisation reduces any procedure to a randomised rule on the total count, and each null rate's maximal certification probability becomes a discrete moment problem whose primal and dual solutions give exact rational certificates. For independent clusters it gives a strong criterion with unrestricted intracluster dependence and moment and Bernstein audits when average intracluster correlation is bounded.
aI4Dxf0xSG.key_idea: Reduce certification under r-wise independence to a discrete moment problem on the total count and read exact minimum sample sizes from primal-dual certificates.
aI4Dxf0xSG.evidence: Exact theory with applications to clinical referral, spacecraft telemetry and language model reliability (including 9,000 generations from 180 prompts per a review).
aI4Dxf0xSG.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically; the abstract reports exact minimum sample requirements for randomised rules and certified deterministic gates and a scaling law across independence orders.
aI4Dxf0xSG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree dependence in evaluation is a practical, important problem and that the theory yields exact minimum sample sizes with verifiable certificates and diverse applications.
aI4Dxf0xSG.main_concern: The guarantees depend on dependence assumptions (r-wise independence, common Bernoulli marginals) that are hard to verify, and the audits are conservative, abstaining in some cases where the true rate meets the target.

6fhgvV3yZA.one_liner: Query-time open-vocabulary Gaussian splatting segmentation treating views as noisy annotators, fitting a per-query binomial mixture by EM without labels.
6fhgvV3yZA.problem: Pre-query feature lifting mixes observations before their query relevance is known, constrains extent with predefined groups, and uses tuned thresholds that ignore query-specific score distributions.
6fhgvV3yZA.method: VerdictGS aggregates per-view text-mask responses onto Gaussians, fits a per-query two-population binomial mixture with EM to infer membership evidence with an adaptive decision boundary (and an empty output when the object is absent), and fuses evidence across mask granularities. It builds no language representation before the query.
6fhgvV3yZA.key_idea: Score each view's masks against the query first, then infer Gaussian membership from a label-free two-component binomial mixture fitted per query via EM.
6fhgvV3yZA.evidence: Three benchmarks including LERF-OVS and ScanNet (per reviews), controlled comparisons with feature aggregation under identical inputs, ablations, and an efficiency analysis on one scene.
6fhgvV3yZA.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically in the visible abstract, which claims no pre-query features, object groups or tuned thresholds.
6fhgvV3yZA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that scoring masks against the query within each view before lifting is a principled idea supported by controlled comparisons on all three benchmarks.
6fhgvV3yZA.main_concern: The per-query mixture adds little over simpler rules (per-query Otsu thresholding beat it on both benchmarks compared), and query-time cost and memory scaling are untested beyond one small scene.

gINwr4UNcl.one_liner: Consistency training enforcing agreement across non-canonical retokenizations of a prompt to resist adversarial tokenization while outputs stay canonical.
gINwr4UNcl.problem: Models trained on canonical tokenization are only partly invariant to non-canonical tokenizations of the same bytes, so byte-identical prompts can yield divergent behavior and adversarial tokenizations can bypass safety alignment.
gINwr4UNcl.method: It gives a mechanistic account of the fragility and trains with a consistency objective that enforces agreement across retokenizations of the prompt while the output space stays canonically tokenized. Probing shows the attack suppresses a linearly decodable safety readout in the residual stream, which consistency training restores.
gINwr4UNcl.key_idea: Train the model so representations or outputs for different tokenizations of the same prompt agree, restoring the suppressed linear safety readout.
gINwr4UNcl.evidence: Three model families, residual-stream probing, and safety evaluations mainly on OLMo-2-7B-Instruct with a single training seed (per reviews).
gINwr4UNcl.claimed_gains: Not stated numerically; trained models are more robust to adversarial tokenization at some loss of benchmark accuracy.
gINwr4UNcl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mechanistic study is careful and interesting and that consistency training substantially lowers adversarial-tokenization attack success.
gINwr4UNcl.main_concern: Safety results come from one model with one training seed and an imperfect judge, so generalization and the capability cost of consistency training remain unclear.

0KUMeXzFw4.one_liner: Hybrid humanoid model: a time-conditioned image world model predicts goal images that steer a goal-conditioned VLA feeding a whole-body controller.
0KUMeXzFw4.problem: VLAs follow training trajectories blindly on out-of-domain tasks, while world models generalize better but are too slow for real-time humanoid loco-manipulation.
0KUMeXzFw4.method: A time-conditioned image world model predicts a future goal image from a time horizon and a language instruction; a re-purposed VLA conditioned on the current observation and the goal image outputs actions that steer the humanoid toward it; a real-time pipeline streams actions to a whole-body controller.
0KUMeXzFw4.key_idea: Steer a VLA with a world-model-generated future goal image conditioned on a time horizon, separating slow image prediction from fast action generation.
0KUMeXzFw4.evidence: Real-world humanoid experiments on five long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, in-domain and out-of-domain, compared with two VLAs and two world-action models per reviews, plus predictor ablations.
0KUMeXzFw4.claimed_gains: Enables up to five minutes of autonomous execution on long-horizon whole-body loco-manipulation tasks; no success-rate numbers are given in the visible abstract.
0KUMeXzFw4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the full system is mature and effective in real-world humanoid experiments, with strong results on in-domain and out-of-domain tasks.
0KUMeXzFw4.main_concern: Comparisons with other visual-goal methods such as SuSIE are missing and there is no downstream evidence that the time-conditioned predictor improves closed-loop control, and the work is viewed as a combination of existing components.

ogCWEINKKm.one_liner: Supervises a driving vision-language model with current and future 4D occupancy, then aligns trajectories with reinforcement learning.
ogCWEINKKm.problem: Driving VLA models are trained mainly on language answers or expert trajectories, giving little supervision to the intermediate representations linking perception to decisions, which may encourage shortcut learning.
ogCWEINKKm.method: PhysDrive adds training-time occupancy supervision: current occupancy grounds 3D geometry and future occupancy guides modeling of physical evolution. A second-stage RL framework aligns generated trajectories with safety, drivable-area compliance, and progress.
ogCWEINKKm.key_idea: Use current-occupancy and future-occupancy prediction as structured training-time supervision on internal representations before the model produces answers or trajectories.
ogCWEINKKm.evidence: Experiments on NuInstruct and other benchmarks (list truncated in the abstract); reviewers note Qwen2.5-VL at 3B and 7B, with RL and main ablations mostly on 3B.
ogCWEINKKm.claimed_gains: Not stated in the available abstract; a review cites Table 4, where adding future occupancy lowers collision rate from 0.29% to 0.22% and intersection rate from 1.85% to 1.42%.
ogCWEINKKm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining spatial and temporal occupancy supervision is well motivated and that future occupancy improves collision-related metrics.
ogCWEINKKm.main_concern: The role of grounding is not isolated: no same-backbone baseline without grounding plus the same RL, occupancy quality is assessed only qualitatively, and generality beyond Qwen2.5-VL is untested.

HF7HXJsUGx.one_liner: Anytime-valid set-level certificate decides each self-improvement round from a random-order partial read of the score table.
HF7HXJsUGx.problem: Scoring every candidate on every task makes each round of a self-improving program expensive, while deciding from a small sample risks keeping the wrong program.
HF7HXJsUGx.method: BranchCert reads all candidates and the shared parent along one random task order, so the tasks read form a uniform sample, and stops once the round resolves to Accept, None Better, or Undecided. A second form reuses scores from earlier rounds to predict the current batch and tests only the residual.
HF7HXJsUGx.key_idea: Reads candidates and parent along one shared random task order (uniform sample) for anytime-valid stopping; tests only the residual of a history-based prediction.
HF7HXJsUGx.evidence: Public evaluation tables, recorded rounds of a running self-improvement loop, and live re-executions; reviewers mention HELM tables, Qwen 3.5-9B chains, and a theorem bounding wrong verdicts under adaptive stopping.
HF7HXJsUGx.claimed_gains: The abstract gives no figures (text truncated); reviews cite reading 38.2% of the HELM tables and 23.2% of the Qwen 3.5-9B chain table, falling to 19.4% with history.
HF7HXJsUGx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the set-level certificate with Accept, None Better, and Undecided verdicts and guarantees under adaptive stopping is principled and reduces the cells read.
HF7HXJsUGx.main_concern: Gains over baselines are not isolated and practical savings are unclear: baselines lack the lazy-parent set-level wrapper, savings over the exact certificate are modest, and wall-clock and token cost are not reported.

gPGnc81k3P.one_liner: Chooses loop count and chain-of-thought length for looped LMs under a compute budget using answer-settling measurements.
gPGnc81k3P.problem: In looped language models a fixed inference budget must be split between more loops and longer chains of thought, and each extra loop raises both prompt-processing and per-token generation cost.
gPGnc81k3P.method: SETTLE measures when intermediate answers stop changing, separately from whether they are correct, and uses a small labelled calibration set to select a loop count and chain-of-thought token limit under an average compute budget. Budget-conditioned self-distillation is added on top.
gPGnc81k3P.key_idea: Estimate when a looped model's answer settles per model and task, then use a calibration set to pick loop count and CoT token limit under an average budget.
gPGnc81k3P.evidence: Six models from the Ouro, Huginn, and Recurrent-Llama families on ten reasoning benchmarks, with a bound on selection loss in terms of accuracy-estimation error and ablations of estimation, budget sharing, and validation.
gPGnc81k3P.claimed_gains: At half the baseline cost SETTLE-H is 9.8 points more accurate than token-only allocation where both are feasible, reaches baseline accuracy at a median of 68% of baseline cost, and self-distillation adds 36 points on GSM8K at a 32-token budget.
gPGnc81k3P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study of the depth versus chain-length trade-off across six models and ten tasks is systematic and the joint allocation saves compute, with clear writing.
gPGnc81k3P.main_concern: The settling estimator's own contribution is unclear: most gains come from task-level allocation, and it beats direct accuracy lookup by only about 0.1 points, with the advantage vanishing at 50 or more labelled examples.

0T6Adl0o4z.one_liner: Maps each tool to a special token, learns directed tool dependencies in the LLM, and trains with on-policy context distillation.
0T6Adl0o4z.problem: Existing methods inject tool graphs into LLMs through retrieval, serialization, or prompts, producing plans that violate dependency constraints and drift after an early wrong tool choice.
0T6Adl0o4z.method: GRAFT assigns each tool node a dedicated special token and learns directed dependencies in representation space via graph-token edge reconstruction. On-policy tool context distillation then trains the model on its own sampled trajectories with stepwise planning signals from a teacher.
0T6Adl0o4z.key_idea: Tool nodes become special tokens whose directed successors are learned by edge reconstruction, followed by on-policy distillation from a teacher given reference subtasks and tool sequences.
0T6Adl0o4z.evidence: Experiments on tool-planning benchmarks and end-to-end real-world workflows (abstract truncated), with ToolGen as a comparison and ablations of the components.
0T6Adl0o4z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that internalizing directed tool dependencies through graph tokens and combining edge reconstruction with on-policy distillation is well motivated and clearly presented.
0T6Adl0o4z.main_concern: The source of the distillation gains is unclear because the teacher sees reference subtasks and ground-truth tool sequences, so on-policy benefit is not separated from privileged supervision.

Q1GbB864EY.one_liner: Benchmark combining leave-one-out, Shapley and Banzhaf attribution with controlled interventions to test what agent contribution measures in LLM multi-agent systems.
Q1GbB864EY.problem: It is unclear which agent drives the success of an LLM multi-agent system, since aggregate performance cannot answer it and attribution does not simply identify the most capable reasoner.
Q1GbB864EY.method: MASContributionBench covers seven architectures and seven task suites and applies leave-one-out, sampled Shapley, and sampled Banzhaf attribution alongside controlled interventions on communication topology, role prompts, and runtime permissions.
Q1GbB864EY.key_idea: Intervene on topology, role prompts, and runtime permissions and recompute attribution to show contribution depends on execution context rather than intrinsic agent capability.
Q1GbB864EY.evidence: Seven architectures and seven task suites with a single pinned open-weights backbone, fixed tasks, seeds, decoding, and evaluators, plus audits of the realized executions (from reviews).
Q1GbB864EY.claimed_gains: No performance gain is claimed; the abstract reports that changing Coder write access leaves 87.8% of outcomes unchanged and that granting Verifier final-answer authority yields no Verifier-selected outputs in all runs.
Q1GbB864EY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the broad coverage of architectures, attribution methods, and interventions, and the careful control and checking that interventions work as intended.
Q1GbB864EY.main_concern: Generality and novelty are limited: all results use one backbone with single-pass execution, overlap with prior removal-based attribution work, and no downstream use such as pruning agents is shown.

xaBNUUDT19.one_liner: Training-free layer that reuses latent subgoal drafts while execution matches them and bypasses decomposition when the goal is reachable.
xaBNUUDT19.problem: Hierarchical latent world-model planners regenerate subgoals at every replanning step and decompose every goal by fixed schedule, even when the previous draft is still consistent or the executor could reach the goal directly.
xaBNUUDT19.method: Surveyor sits between an executor and a frozen world model: a drafter proposes latent subgoals ahead, an accept rule reuses the draft while the achieved latent state agrees with the subgoal being pursued, and an arbiter bypasses or retires drafting once the goal is predicted to be within reach. Tolerance is calibrated offline from observation pairs the benchmark treats as equivalent.
xaBNUUDT19.key_idea: Gate subgoal regeneration by latent agreement with the subgoal being pursued and gate decomposition by predicted reachability, with an offline-calibrated tolerance.
xaBNUUDT19.evidence: Five executors (sampling-based, gradient-based, and amortized planners) across four environments, with extensive ablations.
xaBNUUDT19.claimed_gains: Raises success at the longest PushT goal distance from below 10% to above 92% for every search-based executor.
xaBNUUDT19.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically meaningful, the method is simple, training-free, and pluggable into various planners, and the experiments and ablations are broad.
xaBNUUDT19.main_concern: Novelty is limited relative to FF-JEPA and AdaReP-style event-triggered replanning, and reduced subgoal calls do not translate into consistent end-to-end compute savings, with slower runs on half the tasks.

UTn7od84C1.one_liner: Steiner-point level method gets LR^2/N^3 rate (up to logs) for smooth convex minimization over the l1 ball.
UTn7od84C1.problem: With only Euclidean smoothness on the l1 ball, accelerated methods reach O(LR^2/N^2) while the Guzman-Nemirovski lower bound is order LR^2/N^3, and whether the upper bound could match it was a question of Nemirovski.
UTn7od84C1.method: A level method keeps every supporting hyperplane seen as a level cut and queries near the Steiner point of the resulting localization polytope. A matching lower bound is shown for deterministic and randomized methods in dimension proportional to the number of queries.
UTn7od84C1.key_idea: Query near the Steiner point of the polytope of accumulated level cuts, exploiting that Steiner points move only polylogarithmically in dimension along nested subsets of the ball.
UTn7od84C1.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower bounds; a review notes experiments that also report substantial computational costs and configurations with little improvement.
UTn7od84C1.claimed_gains: The minimax gap is of order LR^2/N^3 up to logarithmic factors, versus O(LR^2/N^2) for the accelerated method with a Euclidean prox-setup.
UTn7od84C1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that nearly matching oracle-complexity bounds closing the N^-2 versus N^-3 gap are a meaningful, clearly presented result with a clean Steiner-path mechanism.
UTn7od84C1.main_concern: Concurrent work (Martinez-Rubio et al., Martinez-Rubio and Guzman, Ouyang) obtains overlapping rates and uses similar Steiner-point mechanisms, so the headline novelty needs qualification.

G2OzTLXfSh.one_liner: Shows fast low-precision matrix multiplication can break prefix invariance and constructs certified two-level Strassen realizations on integer codes.
G2OzTLXfSh.problem: Fast matrix multiplication that rounds sums mixing token rows can let later tokens affect earlier LLM outputs, violating prefix invariance that accuracy checks do not detect.
G2OzTLXfSh.method: Constructs realizations of two-level Strassen on bounded integer codes that quantize token rows independently, then mix and cancel exactly before rescaling, using 49 block multiplications instead of 64, with a certificate guaranteeing bitwise equality to a row-local classical int8 operator.
G2OzTLXfSh.key_idea: Quantize rows independently and perform Strassen mixing and cancellation exactly in integer arithmetic before rescaling, so outputs equal a row-local int8 operator bitwise.
G2OzTLXfSh.evidence: Suffix-replacement tests on Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct with OpenBookQA likelihood scoring and NQ-open batched answering, plus a sweep of 512 sign variants of two-level Strassen.
G2OzTLXfSh.claimed_gains: Existing fast FP8 realizations change answers on 4.17-10.00% of OpenBookQA items and 39.6-51.8% of NQ-open questions, teacher-forced perplexities across 512 variants span a 772.4x range, and certified realizations use 49 instead of 64 block multiplications.
G2OzTLXfSh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the suffix-replacement experiments with row-local controls convincing that accuracy alone misses prefix-invariance failures, and the certificate a concrete remedy.
G2OzTLXfSh.main_concern: Certified realizations show no practical speedup (the two-level kernel is 27.9x slower than classical int8) and gain invariance only by reproducing int8 exactly, with failures shown only in the authors' own FP8 compositions.

eC7MH5DgcU.one_liner: Measures tool-schema bias by rewriting tool schemas with nine executable operators, then tests SFT and GRPO as mitigations.
eC7MH5DgcU.problem: LLM agents perform very differently across functionally equivalent tool schemas, so results on one fixed schema do not show the agent has learned the task.
eC7MH5DgcU.method: An executable transformation framework rewrites native tool schemas with nine operators (merging and splitting tools, changing how one tool is expressed, spreading an action over dependent calls) while keeping tasks, executable actions, and reachable states fixed. It evaluates eleven LLMs on up to 32 variants, tests whether difficulty can be predicted from a small sample, and tests whether training removes the bias.
eC7MH5DgcU.key_idea: Rewrites tool schemas with equivalence-verified executable operators that keep tasks, native actions, and reachable states fixed, so success changes are attributable to the interface alone.
eC7MH5DgcU.evidence: Eleven LLMs (two closed) on up to 32 schema variants; SFT and GRPO mitigation experiments on Qwen3-4B only (per reviews); about fifty thousand reference-trajectory equivalence checks (per reviews).
eC7MH5DgcU.claimed_gains: Schema bias is substantial: success rates range from complete failure to 97% depending solely on the schema; no mitigation numbers appear in the visible abstract.
eC7MH5DgcU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the executable, equivalence-verified framework that fixes tasks and actions, and the broad measurement across eleven models and many schema variants.
eC7MH5DgcU.main_concern: Equivalence is only at the execution level, so some measured gaps may reflect harder or less readable interfaces rather than bias, and mitigation experiments cover only Qwen3-4B.

fbREWUeVcY.one_liner: SingDance composes separately learned lip-sync and music-driven dance in one video diffusion model to generate singing-and-dancing zero-shot.
fbREWUeVcY.problem: Music-conditioned dance methods ignore vocal articulation and speech-driven models assume the visible subject produces the voice, leaving singing-and-dancing video generation underexplored.
fbREWUeVcY.method: A unified video diffusion framework that defines vocal articulation as a semantic role (source or listener), with task-defined hard-compact routing selecting speech, music, and role conditions composed by frame-wise joint audio injection. Training uses asymmetric supervision (speaking and listening videos for role control, dancing-only videos for body motion) and holds out the Song/Source configuration.
fbREWUeVcY.key_idea: Train articulation and music-conditioned dance from separate data under a source/listener role, then assign the source role to a song at inference to compose both.
fbREWUeVcY.evidence: Held-out Song/Source zero-shot evaluation, a comparison with Wan-S2V for singing-and-dancing, ablations of music conditioning and condition control, and vocal-role interventions (abstract cut off).
fbREWUeVcY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the compositional singing-and-dancing formulation is interesting, handles four tasks in one model, and that role interventions show lip sync can be controlled while keeping music-aligned body motion.
fbREWUeVcY.main_concern: Compositional generalization is shown on a single held-out configuration with Wan-S2V as the only baseline, and ablations do not isolate routing or staged training or include a cascaded dance-then-lip-sync baseline.

7YXKKMgXl2.one_liner: The readout, not the score, decides which modern Hopfield networks have a constant-metric energy; gradient readouts admit convex-plus-quadratic scores.
7YXKKMgXl2.problem: Frameworks that generalise the score and weighting of modern Hopfield networks keep the weighted-average pattern readout, and it is unclear which scores give each retrieval step an energy in a constant metric.
7YXKKMgXl2.method: They define a constant-metric energy through a concave-convex step, characterize splitting scores under the pattern readout, show that the gradient readout (gradient of a potential of the scores) gives such an energy for every score convex up to an added quadratic, and audit 32 published retrieval maps.
7YXKKMgXl2.key_idea: Use the gradient of the score's potential as readout, making each retrieval step a concave-convex step on a constant-metric energy for scores convex up to a quadratic.
7YXKKMgXl2.evidence: Theorems on splitting scores and gradient readouts, an audit of 32 published retrieval maps, and a multiple-instance-learning experiment with the adaptive Hopfield network (abstract cut off).
7YXKKMgXl2.claimed_gains: Among 32 published retrieval maps, 8 have no constant-metric energy at a tested configuration and no energy proved in their own papers; no performance gain is stated.
7YXKKMgXl2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical characterization is rigorous and general, giving usable criteria for when Hopfield-style retrieval maps are well behaved and a retrospective analysis of prior designs.
7YXKKMgXl2.main_concern: Practical relevance is unclear and the writing is hard to follow: the energy guarantee has not been shown to improve retrieval quality or multiple-instance-learning stability, and the fix adds computational cost.

3J14rTUf07.one_liner: Groups recommendation experiences by reward, continuation probability, and successor features, then constrains critic updates to limit loss increases per group.
3J14rTUf07.problem: Sharing one value function across users with heterogeneous interaction dynamics lets one user's update distort others' value estimates, and the errors propagate through TD targets.
3J14rTUf07.method: Heterogeneity-Aware Experience Grouping estimates expected reward, continuation probability, and successor-state features to group experiences; Transfer-Constrained Value Learning minimally adjusts proposed critic updates subject to reference TD-loss constraints defined by these groups.
3J14rTUf07.key_idea: Group transitions by Bellman-backup compatibility and minimally adjust each critic update so reference TD loss on each group does not rise beyond a tolerance.
