3J14rTUf07.evidence: A local bound on group-level reference-loss increases, experiments on real-world recommendation datasets, and per reviews a simulator-based offline evaluation plus a seven-day online test.
3J14rTUf07.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract reports consistent cumulative-reward improvements on real-world recommendation datasets.
3J14rTUf07.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find grouping by reward and transition features, rather than scalar value, a principled improvement, backed by a solid theoretical connection to Bellman-backup discrepancy and supportive ablations.
3J14rTUf07.main_concern: Gains over the strongest non-HAVL comparator are only about 1-2% against added per-update cost and many hyperparameters reported at one calibrated configuration, with limited evidence of long-term user benefit.

9TLNhvwnNa.one_liner: Inverse theory that sets residual initialization scale from a target fraction of inactive features, rather than from activation variance.
9TLNhvwnNa.problem: Controlling activation variance does not determine how many features are zero on every input, and such features contribute no signal to a linear readout on that input set.
9TLNhvwnNa.method: For Gaussian residual branches followed by a terminal ReLU, it proves convergence of the joint empirical feature law as width and depth grow at arbitrary relative rates and derives unique inverses for marginal inactivity and, for ReLU or leaky ReLU, joint inactivity. It also constructs non-Gaussian input laws with identical pairwise terminal feature distributions but different unused-feature fractions.
9TLNhvwnNa.key_idea: Invert the limiting joint feature law to choose the residual scale that yields a prescribed fraction of inactive features.
9TLNhvwnNa.evidence: Proofs in the joint width-depth limit with finite branch width, plus experiments verifying calibration and predicted fitting differences; a short classification experiment shows no consistent accuracy difference per reviewers.
9TLNhvwnNa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the inverse problem is solved rigorously in a joint width-depth limit and that experiments support the predictions at finite widths and depths.
9TLNhvwnNa.main_concern: Practical significance is limited: controlling initial inactivity is not shown to matter after training since silent features can reactivate and accuracy shows no consistent gain, and the setting (single terminal ReLU, no normalization) is special.

zG4PjX4uw0.one_liner: Replaces direct Q-functions with a pretrained latent dynamics model composed with a state-value model to refine robot policies online.
zG4PjX4uw0.problem: Offline-initialized Q-functions are unreliable on the nearby unseen actions introduced during online RL refinement of pretrained imitation policies.
zG4PjX4uw0.method: An action chunk is scored by predicting its latent successor with a pretrained latent dynamics model adapted on task offline transitions, then scoring that state with a value model initialized from task-progress supervision. Online, new transitions update the dynamics model, TD learning calibrates the value, and policy gradients flow through the composition; it is instantiated with DINO-WM and RoboMeter.
zG4PjX4uw0.key_idea: Evaluate an action chunk as a state value of its predicted latent successor, so the evaluator generalizes locally to action perturbations during refinement.
zG4PjX4uw0.evidence: Precise manipulation tasks in simulation (MimicGen per reviews) and the real world, with the evaluator replacing Q-functions in residual and latent-steering refinement methods and compared with Q-based baselines such as DICE-RL and DSRL.
zG4PjX4uw0.claimed_gains: Improves online sample efficiency over the corresponding Q-based methods; no numbers stated.
zG4PjX4uw0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and the evaluator is a drop-in replacement that improves performance over Q-based baselines in simulation and real-robot experiments.
zG4PjX4uw0.main_concern: The gain is not isolated from the use of pretrained components and extra supervision, since the composed evaluator and a Q-function can represent the same functions, and comparisons to prior similar decompositions are missing.

s5T8BuR68X.one_liner: Trains an ordered image code whose early prefixes are supervised by successively summarized captions, so words come first.
s5T8BuR68X.problem: Pixel-reconstruction training makes early code units preserve appearance, which need not capture a prompt's objects, counts or relations.
s5T8BuR68X.method: Formulates captioning and text-to-image generation as successive refinement under a distortion schedule, with early stages predicting captions and the last reconstructing pixels. RUNG supervises code prefixes with successively summarized captions; generation extends the code, captioning truncates it, and correction redraws a block whose prefix fails a prompt check.
s5T8BuR68X.key_idea: A ladder of successively summarized captions supervises ordered code prefixes, making language the low-rate prefix of the visual code.
s5T8BuR68X.evidence: Matched architecture, data and capacity retraining comparisons, a retrained FlexTok tokenizer, GenEval and DPG-Bench evaluations, caption recovery from partial codes, reconstruction cost, human raters, and propositions on rate-optimality.
s5T8BuR68X.claimed_gains: Language ordering raises GenEval from 0.76 to 0.83, a quarter of the code recovers 88.7% of reference attribute tuples versus 31.4%, and RUNG-XL (3.4B) reaches 0.88 GenEval and 87.6 DPG-Bench in 32 network evaluations, 0.91 GenEval with correction.
s5T8BuR68X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea of choosing what early code prefixes represent is compelling and that the theory yields testable consequences supported by controlled ordering comparisons.
s5T8BuR68X.main_concern: Some claims exceed the evidence: an unexplained 9-point GenEval gap versus FlexTok, estimated information bounds that may not be valid lower bounds, a correction process that relies on its own internal checker, and writing that is hard for outsiders to follow.

cUmXESNRPQ.one_liner: Fully hyperbolic vision transformer reformulated in polar coordinates to avoid numerical cancellation in Lorentz operations at large radii.
cUmXESNRPQ.problem: Lorentz transformer blocks in ambient coordinates suffer numerical errors at large radii, forcing models to limit the radius and forgo the hierarchy-embedding benefits of hyperbolic space.
cUmXESNRPQ.method: Revisits transformer components in polar coordinates with a polar fully-connected layer that maps direction and radius separately, horospherical shifts as relative positional encodings, and residual connections reformulated as Lorentz boosts. Distances and attention centroids are computed without the cancellation of ambient formulations.
cUmXESNRPQ.key_idea: Separating direction and radius in polar coordinates makes distances and centroids stable at large radii, with Lorentz boosts as isometric residual connections at any radius.
cUmXESNRPQ.evidence: Standard vision tasks including CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet against Euclidean and hyperbolic baselines per reviews, trained for 100 epochs with the HexFormer recipe.
cUmXESNRPQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the numerical-stability motivation is clear and well analyzed and that Polar-ViT outperforms the reported Euclidean and hyperbolic baselines.
cUmXESNRPQ.main_concern: Limited evidence and novelty: no causal evidence that improved stability drives the gains (no per-layer radius distributions), small-scale experiments, few hyperbolic baselines, and components seen as incremental over prior Lorentz work.

d1whGKSocr.one_liner: Asynchronous incremental vertical federated multi-view clustering where each arriving client uploads a label matrix and the server updates one consensus.
d1whGKSocr.problem: Existing vertical federated multi-view clustering assumes all clients are available at once and requires earlier clients to participate again, which is infeasible or costly when clients join asynchronously and old clients leave.
d1whGKSocr.method: Each arriving client builds an anchor graph from its own view and learns a local label matrix that is uploaded to the server. The server and the current client alternately update the global consensus and the local label matrix through an augmented Lagrangian formulation until convergence, so only the current client participates and only the latest consensus is stored.
d1whGKSocr.key_idea: Fuse the stored consensus and each new client's label matrix by alternating augmented-Lagrangian updates, so previous clients never participate again and the server stores only the latest consensus.
d1whGKSocr.evidence: Experiments on multiple datasets confirm applicability in incremental scenarios; reviewers note ACC improvements on several datasets and short convergence plots.
d1whGKSocr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the setting of clients joining one at a time and never returning is realistic and under-studied, and that server storage does not grow with the number of past clients.
d1whGKSocr.main_concern: The server objective is not well defined (Eq. 2 penalizes only distance to previous iterates, Eq. 25 weights become 0/0 at convergence, cluster-label alignment is unspecified), with no convergence guarantee.

hBON0pPV15.one_liner: Pre-trains a diffusion model on reward-relabeled exploratory data, then steers it with a lightweight guidance model to augment RL buffers.
hBON0pPV15.problem: Generative replay for RL normally needs task rewards, but it is unclear how to reuse pre-collected unlabeled exploratory data when the downstream reward cannot be queried on it.
hBON0pPV15.method: UGR pre-trains a diffusion model on exploratory transitions relabeled with diverse reward priors to serve as unsupervised generative priors. For a specific task, it trains only a lightweight guidance model to steer generation toward the target task.
hBON0pPV15.key_idea: Separate a reusable, reward-prior-conditioned diffusion pre-training stage from a small task-specific guidance model that steers generated transitions toward the downstream reward.
hBON0pPV15.evidence: Complex control tasks on DeepMind Control Suite (12 continuous-control tasks per a reviewer) under a fixed interaction budget, compared with REDQ, SynthER, PGR, and Relabel-REDQ.
hBON0pPV15.claimed_gains: Improves online data efficiency under a fixed interaction budget; no numbers stated.
hBON0pPV15.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the setting is well motivated, the method section is clear, and UGR gives reasonably large gains over PGR and SynthER with ablations showing sensitivity.
hBON0pPV15.main_concern: Baselines are not matched on data: UGR uses a large pretraining dataset while REDQ, SynthER, and PGR use only online data, and obvious baselines (pretrained SynthER or PGR, RLPD-style mixing) are missing.

M1hTi1kT2J.one_liner: Two-stage Chinese labor dispute cases and directional departure metrics benchmark employer-versus-employee positional bias in LLM legal adjudication.
M1hTi1kT2J.problem: Standard legal LLM evaluations measure overall agreement with human adjudicators while overlooking whether model disagreements systematically favor employers or employees.
M1hTi1kT2J.method: Adjudex-Labor uses paired real Chinese labor arbitration decisions and subsequent court judgments to separate overall human-model disagreement rates from asymmetric employer- and employee-favoring departure rates and monetary award gaps. It also tests sequential pipelines where model-generated arbitration outcomes replace human arbitration inputs in subsequent court judgments.
M1hTi1kT2J.key_idea: Decompose legal LLM deviations from human arbitral and judicial references into overall disagreement rates versus directional employer- or employee-favoring departure rates across two-stage disputes.
M1hTi1kT2J.evidence: Evaluates multiple LLMs and reasoning configurations on 196 paired Chinese labor arbitration and judicial cases plus a 50-case monetary award subset.
M1hTi1kT2J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating directional party-favoring departures from raw agreement rates reveals an important distributive bias dimension using real two-stage legal disputes.
M1hTi1kT2J.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing benchmark data and code for independent auditing, alongside confounds from court-record evidence summaries, stricter evidentiary thresholds, and label anchoring in sequential evaluation.

igRGXSgcwT.one_liner: Tiered full-precision/INT2 window retention with query-selective fused-kernel reads and window-level completion compresses long-context KV caches.
igRGXSgcwT.problem: Long-context LLM decoding faces heavy KV-cache memory and bandwidth costs because historical token utility evolves broadly and gradually whereas relevance to an individual query is concentrated.
igRGXSgcwT.method: QEvict routes historical KV windows under a byte budget across execution-precision storage, write-once INT2 storage, and permanent eviction using accumulated attention. At query time, a compact selector chooses a fraction of INT2 windows for token-level attention through a fused mixed-precision kernel while representing unread windows via calibrated window-level completion.
igRGXSgcwT.key_idea: Decouple KV-cache retention from per-step reads by storing historical windows in tiered full-precision and INT2 memory while selectively attending to query-relevant INT2 windows with window-level completion.
igRGXSgcwT.evidence: Evaluated on LongBench, RULER, and GSM8K with Llama and Mistral models against eviction, quantization, and mixed-precision KV-cache baselines.
igRGXSgcwT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating broad tiered KV retention from selective query-conditioned INT2 access is well motivated and backed by a practical fused kernel and byte-budgeted evaluations.
igRGXSgcwT.main_concern: Reviewers note high system complexity from combining existing eviction, quantization, and sparse-access components, evaluation on only two 7B–8B models, and weaker default accuracy than pure quantization baselines on GSM8K.

Ai689rllCI.one_liner: Task-native sentinel monitoring triggers budgeted certificate-margin hinge penalties to protect eroding capabilities during LLM preference optimization.
Ai689rllCI.problem: Preference optimization unevenly erodes critical capabilities such as safety even as average multi-task scores and internal likelihood margins rise, causing global anchoring or margin monitors to miss or over-penalize updates.
Ai689rllCI.method: RETAINPO evaluates task-native sentinel questions during training to detect statistically supported per-capability losses and allocates a capped token budget to the most degraded capabilities, abstaining when no loss is supported. A hinge loss on the likelihood margins of verified certificates from those affected capabilities is then added to the preference objective.
Ai689rllCI.key_idea: Detect capability-specific degradation via task-native sentinel evaluations and selectively apply a capped-budget likelihood-margin hinge penalty on verified certificates only for capabilities with statistically supported loss.
Ai689rllCI.evidence: Evaluated across three seeds on full-parameter DPO and SimPO of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct tracking six capabilities against anchoring and static-allocation baselines.
Ai689rllCI.claimed_gains: Across three seeds, RETAINPO restores held-out safety from 92.5 to 97.0 percent at preference accuracy comparable to DPO while retaining its truthfulness gain.
Ai689rllCI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a valuable monitoring failure—rising likelihood margins alongside falling held-out safety—that motivates separating erosion detection from retention penalties.
Ai689rllCI.main_concern: Reviewers point out that dynamic allocation uses more retention tokens than static baselines under SimPO while performing similarly to static allocation under DPO, and that experiments use only Qwen2.5-1.5B.

MQlrVKfBqX.one_liner: Distilled symbol-level HMM look-ahead weights candidate tokens by safe-completion probability to enforce formal safety rules in single-pass LLM planning.
MQlrVKfBqX.problem: Language-model robot planners can output executable, goal-reaching plans that violate formal safety rules, while rejection sampling frequently fails to find safe plans.
MQlrVKfBqX.method: GUARDCTRL distills a hidden Markov model over grounded action and object symbols to track world states and formal rule progress across hypothetical continuations. Weighting each candidate token by the exact HMM probability of completing into a safe plan guarantees safety in one decoding pass when a safe plan exists within the horizon while preserving LLM preferences.
MQlrVKfBqX.key_idea: Weight candidate tokens during single-pass decoding by exact safe-plan completion probabilities computed via a distilled symbol-level HMM tracking world transitions and formal safety rules.
MQlrVKfBqX.evidence: Evaluated with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct against ten-attempt rejection sampling and GPT-5 on the DESPITE benchmark and a benchmark with temporal rules over action history.
MQlrVKfBqX.claimed_gains: With Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, GUARDCTRL is safe on 98.4% of DESPITE hard tasks and 98.2% of temporal-rule tasks versus 13.8% and 6.4% for up-to-ten-attempt rejection sampling, taking about twice the time of one unconstrained generation.
MQlrVKfBqX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate integrating formal symbolic world and rule monitoring with LLM planning and cleanly separating look-ahead support (safety guarantee) from magnitude (preference preservation).
MQlrVKfBqX.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments do not isolate probabilistic HMM token weighting against an unweighted exact safe-support binary shield or classical search with LLM reranking.

DVeocDmZ5Q.one_liner: Tokenizer initialization, freezing, and semantic weight reuse reveal conditions for transferring pretrained physics representations.
DVeocDmZ5Q.problem: It remains unclear when pretrained physics tokenizers improve downstream emulation or transfer across physical systems.
DVeocDmZ5Q.method: The study compares scratch-trained emulators with pretrained-tokenizer initialization across pretraining domains and data regimes. It varies tokenizer adaptation and reuses weights from semantically related physical fields.
DVeocDmZ5Q.key_idea: Adapt pretrained tokenizers under domain shift and initialize unseen physical fields with weights from semantically related fields.
DVeocDmZ5Q.evidence: Three physical systems from The Well support next-step, autoregressive rollout, domain-shift, and data-scarcity evaluations.
DVeocDmZ5Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the systematic study of tokenizer pretraining, freezing, and physical-field semantics for downstream emulation.
DVeocDmZ5Q.main_concern: Reviewers identify missing comparisons with relevant prior physics-modeling approaches, limiting assessment of the contribution.

uvjYImnhyr.one_liner: A resistance-to-friction curriculum and pre-slip reward train two arms to open unanchored objects while stabilizing their bodies.
uvjYImnhyr.problem: Opening resistance couples pulling and stabilization because excessive force can move an unanchored object's entire body.
uvjYImnhyr.method: BARS-RL trains a policy to allocate task-arm and support-arm force without observing resistance or friction. A base-slip-boundary penalty and resistance-to-friction curriculum progress from anchored objects to mixed unanchored conditions.
uvjYImnhyr.key_idea: Penalize contact forces near base slip and stage training by resistance-to-friction ratio to learn when support-arm stabilization is necessary.
uvjYImnhyr.evidence: The abstract reports experiments on three simulated revolute- and prismatic-joint objects and real-robot trials across two appliances.
uvjYImnhyr.claimed_gains: BARS-RL achieves 83.5% average simulated success and succeeds in 19 of 20 real-robot trials across two appliances.
uvjYImnhyr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that coupling opening with stabilization is practically meaningful and that the physical ratio motivates a useful curriculum.
uvjYImnhyr.main_concern: Reviewers question the method's advantage over stronger existing bimanual approaches because comparative baselines are limited.

4bndQKp9Fz.one_liner: Parameter-reduced semidefinite searches construct Lyapunov certificates for alternating descent-ascent with negative momentum over broader parameter ranges.
4bndQKp9Fz.problem: Existing convergence guarantees for alternating descent-ascent with negative momentum cover only a particular stepsize and momentum choice.
4bndQKp9Fz.method: The work searches for Lyapunov potentials using parametric semidefinite programs and reduces parameter count to make the search tractable. It proves matching convex-concave bounds and worst-case optimal strongly-convex-strongly-concave rates.
4bndQKp9Fz.key_idea: Reduce parametric Lyapunov-search SDPs and verify exact algebraic certificates across a stepsize-momentum region.
4bndQKp9Fz.evidence: Computer-assisted proofs establish matching upper and lower bounds, with rational certificates checked using Sylvester's criterion and Sturm sequences and simplified Adam experiments.
4bndQKp9Fz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the rigorous analysis extends convergence guarantees and establishes tight dependence on stepsize, momentum, and iteration count.
4bndQKp9Fz.main_concern: Reviewers see the advance as incremental and find its practical significance unclear without stronger minimax-optimizer comparisons.

omlW02KyAz.one_liner: SETSUNET learns curvature-aware search directions that complement a base solver and coordinate recovery across observation views.
omlW02KyAz.problem: Geometric and visual inverse problems require accurate recovery with few optimization updates.
omlW02KyAz.method: A shared graph network derives search directions from local gradients and curvature, projects them to complement a measured base solve, and coordinates them across views. Cholesky whitening accelerates the solver while preserving physical updates and trained weights.
omlW02KyAz.key_idea: Project learned search directions into a complement of the base solve and coordinate their contributions across observation views.
omlW02KyAz.evidence: Whitening-equivariance analysis and experiments cover multiframe and pairwise alignment, stereo, biased-graph estimation, and image restoration, including comparisons with HSLM, Ceres LM, Dogbox, VeLO, and random completion.
omlW02KyAz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the integration of learned search directions with a conventional numerical solver.
omlW02KyAz.main_concern: The contribution of learned directions remains insufficiently isolated through ablations with matched computational budgets.

Ky2kyPpTun.one_liner: SCENE alternates knowledge-guided schema mapping and multi-objective search to produce testable biomedical propositions.
Ky2kyPpTun.problem: Broad biomedical knowledge does not directly map to dataset variables, while dataset-specific patterns often lack mechanistic interpretation.
Ky2kyPpTun.method: SCENE uses an upper agent level to translate biomedical knowledge into dataset-grounded search directions and a lower level to optimize propositions for evidential strength and data support. Feedback from the lower level refines subsequent search directions.
Ky2kyPpTun.key_idea: Iteratively map biomedical priors onto dataset schemas, search for supported propositions, and feed the resulting evidence back into direction selection.
Ky2kyPpTun.evidence: Reviews describe evaluations on two randomized trials and LINCS L1000 with paired splits, held-out replay, and targeted bootstrap controls.
Ky2kyPpTun.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the auditable conversion of broad knowledge into executable propositions with deterministic checks and controlled evaluation splits.
Ky2kyPpTun.main_concern: Subgroup selection using on-treatment variables breaks randomization, undermining causal treatment-benefit interpretations.

USSefl5nra.one_liner: VINEA encodes spectral prominence, branch geometry, and scale-space persistence using persistent homology across spectroscopy modalities.
USSefl5nra.problem: Dense spectral grids entangle chemical information with acquisition artifacts, while sparse peak lists depend on detection thresholds.
USSefl5nra.method: VINEA combines persistent homology, multiscale topological prominence, branch geometry, and scale-space persistence in a shared spectral representation. It calibrates augmentation strengths against measured spectral statistics for transfer to experimental data.
USSefl5nra.key_idea: Represent spectra through persistent topological features and their geometric evolution across scales.
USSefl5nra.evidence: Synthetic corruption benchmarks and experimental-data transfer evaluate proton NMR, HSQC, IR, and Raman, with reviews describing comparisons against 15 retrained encoders.
USSefl5nra.claimed_gains: VINEA uses approximately 1M parameters for its shared spectral representation.
USSefl5nra.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the physically motivated representation and broad, controlled evaluation across spectroscopy modalities.
USSefl5nra.main_concern: Reviewers question whether robustness to synthetic corruptions transfers to real acquisition artifacts and experimental-domain shifts.

6PUsdjv3Eh.one_liner: SPD fuses regularized Normal-Inverse-Gamma predictions and reweights gradients according to predictive distributions for multimodal regression.
6PUsdjv3Eh.problem: Point-wise multimodal regression predictions leave generalization under noisy inputs insufficiently controlled.
6PUsdjv3Eh.method: SPD represents continuous outputs with regularized Normal-Inverse-Gamma distributions and performs multimodal fusion in that distribution space. Distribution-aware reweighting adapts optimization, while conditional analysis relates predictive regularization to capacity control and empirical risk.
6PUsdjv3Eh.key_idea: Regularize Normal-Inverse-Gamma predictive distributions and use their structure to modulate multimodal optimization.
6PUsdjv3Eh.evidence: Conditional generalization-bound analysis accompanies image fusion, crowd counting, and depth estimation experiments with multiple corruption types and component ablations.
6PUsdjv3Eh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the distribution-based framework reasonable and the results across noisy regression tasks promising.
6PUsdjv3Eh.main_concern: The theoretical assumptions and regularizer are not shown to match the implemented training procedure.

aEPJT4hW84.one_liner: Checkpoint interventions cross inherited models, repair procedures, and evidence histories to attribute gains in recursive self-improvement.
aEPJT4hW84.problem: Descendant-performance gains can conflate improvements to a repair procedure with inherited model structure and accessible evidence.
aEPJT4hW84.method: A neuro-symbolic world model allows its repair procedure to edit its successor generator, while checkpoints record model, procedure, history, and evaluation conditions. Crossed interventions compare continued editing with frozen generators and non-recursive selection under controlled evidence histories.
aEPJT4hW84.key_idea: Cross model inheritance, repair procedures, and evidence histories at checkpoints to separate their contributions to descendant performance.
aEPJT4hW84.evidence: The study includes a replication on 252 fresh world families, frozen-transfer equivalence tests, and a separate experiment tracking four lineages in each of 126 families.
aEPJT4hW84.claimed_gains: Factorial contrasts allocate 45% of mean diagonal gain to the inherited procedure and 55% to model structure, while non-recursive selection matches continued editing at the declared margin with 144 versus 192 fits.
aEPJT4hW84.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled attribution framework and its distinction between descendant quality and improver quality.
aEPJT4hW84.main_concern: The restricted synthetic testbed does not establish generalization to established or more complex self-improving agent systems.

wucl3UsEii.one_liner: Latent Transition Alignment preserves cross-layer transition directions with one-sided magnitude control during replay-free language-model continual learning.
wucl3UsEii.problem: Replay-free updates can disrupt existing language-model capabilities, while preservation objectives often ignore cross-layer transformations.
wucl3UsEii.method: An offline dual-anchor surrogate relates observed latent transitions to a latent self-map's residual field. Online training aligns transition directions and applies one-sided magnitude control without field fitting or fixed-point iteration.
wucl3UsEii.key_idea: Preserve realized cross-layer transition directions while allowing shared endpoint shifts and selectively constraining transition magnitudes.
wucl3UsEii.evidence: Exact and approximate reconstruction analyses accompany single-domain and sequential experiments with matched baselines, five paired seeds, multiple task orders, and Qwen2.5 models up to 3B.
wucl3UsEii.claimed_gains: Relative to Output KL, accumulated first-domain forgetting decreases by 8.20, with the unit absent from the truncated abstract.
wucl3UsEii.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate cross-layer transitions as a flexible preservation target and the structural baselines and component ablations.
wucl3UsEii.main_concern: The evaluation does not establish the full retention-adaptation tradeoff across sequentially learned domains.

ml4xqcOZny.one_liner: Equal-budget validation compares skill edits in isolation and library context using edit margins, context distortion, and sampling noise.
ml4xqcOZny.problem: An agent skill edit can behave differently inside its deployment library than in isolated validation.
ml4xqcOZny.method: The study compares isolated and context-matched validation at equal rollout budgets and separates changes in edit effects from changes in acceptance-decision value. Decision-risk analysis relates validator choice to context distortion, edit margins, and sampling noise.
ml4xqcOZny.key_idea: Compare context-induced edit-effect distortion with acceptance margins and finite-sample noise to determine when contextual validation changes decision value.
ml4xqcOZny.evidence: Preregistered ScienceWorld studies include Qwen2.5-14B, 32 independently grown libraries with up to 64 entries and 6,265 guidance tokens, and a separate 64-event study.
ml4xqcOZny.claimed_gains: Matched validation accepts a rewrite with a confirmed 13.05 progress-point deployment gain, while the larger-library study estimates a 0.644-point advantage with a 95% interval spanning zero.
ml4xqcOZny.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the careful experimental controls and the distinction between context-dependent edit effects and validation-decision value.
ml4xqcOZny.main_concern: The narrow tested regimes and weak natural edits limit how broadly the proposed validation-routing rule can generalize.

SuC6hcw1yd.one_liner: Shifted, re-noised action chunks initialize one-step flow-matching VLA inference while preserving the training marginal.
SuC6hcw1yd.problem: One-step VLA action generation can accumulate persistent residual errors that exceed task-dependent closed-loop tolerance.
SuC6hcw1yd.method: Marginal-Aligned Warm Start shifts the previously executed action chunk and re-noises it to the flow's training marginal before taking one denoising step. It requires no training or model-weight changes.
SuC6hcw1yd.key_idea: Shift the previous executed action chunk, re-noise it to the flow-matching marginal, and perform one denoising update.
SuC6hcw1yd.evidence: Experiments span multiple models, simulated benchmarks, and a real robot, with closed-loop residual analysis and comparisons against training-free multi-evaluation baselines.
SuC6hcw1yd.claimed_gains: On π₀, the action head runs 9.1× faster at an unchanged suite average.
SuC6hcw1yd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers describe the method as simple and effective without retraining, supported by simulation and real-robot evaluation.
SuC6hcw1yd.main_concern: The evaluation does not fully establish deployment gains and generality across harder tasks, additional architectures, and end-to-end latency comparisons.

fwuKgiefZ2.one_liner: Frozen defect predictions receive learned preference weights to produce interpretable audio-video quality judgments.
fwuKgiefZ2.problem: Defect detection alone cannot explain human preferences when videos share defects or contain defects of different importance.
fwuKgiefZ2.method: JACE learns defect predictions from incomplete annotations with category-specific refinement, then freezes diagnosis and learns category weights from separate pairwise preferences. Weighted defect contributions combine with a base quality score to predict wins, ties, or losses.
fwuKgiefZ2.key_idea: Freeze a learned defect detector and calibrate its category contributions against pairwise preferences collected on a separate video set.
fwuKgiefZ2.evidence: The supplied reviews report defect-attribution ablations and preference evaluation across generation tasks, while the abstract describes text, image, audio, and video conditioning.
fwuKgiefZ2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating defect diagnosis from preference calibration is well motivated and permits disjoint annotation datasets.
fwuKgiefZ2.main_concern: The evaluation does not adequately establish the reliability and generalization of the attributed preference judgments.

NGw5SOukHy.one_liner: Tool-grounded task generation and reward-gated self-distillation co-train an open-ended agent generator and solver.
NGw5SOukHy.problem: Open-ended agent reinforcement learning lacks scalable verifiable rubrics and suffers from unstable long-horizon reward signals.
NGw5SOukHy.method: ARISE-RL co-evolves a generator that grounds rubrics in tool observations with a solver trained on rubric satisfaction, rewarding valid tasks near the solver's capability boundary. RG-SED distills a memory-augmented policy only when memory empirically improves reward.
NGw5SOukHy.key_idea: Ground generated rubrics in tool observations and gate self-distillation on measured reward improvements from memory-augmented rollouts.
NGw5SOukHy.evidence: ECR-Bench covers single-tool deep research and multi-tool travel planning, and reviewers report evaluations on two model backbones with framework comparisons and ablations.
NGw5SOukHy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the motivation and empirical support for gating self-distillation on useful guidance.
NGw5SOukHy.main_concern: Reliance on the new benchmark and judge-based evaluation leaves benchmark construction, calibration, and evaluation reliability insufficiently established.

24cK0fvWmD.one_liner: Provider and connector hypotheses guide query decomposition, beam-search table composition, and inferred-join traversal for multi-table retrieval.
24cK0fvWmD.problem: Ranking tables independently by query relevance cannot distinguish useful information providers or necessary connectors from redundant candidates.
24cK0fvWmD.method: HCVR decomposes queries into typed requirements and retrieves candidate providers. It composes them through bounded beam search, adds connectors along minimum-hop paths in an inferred join graph, and verifies candidate roles.
24cK0fvWmD.key_idea: Select tables by information-provider or join-connector roles, composing providers with beam search and inserting connectors along inferred minimum-hop join paths.
24cK0fvWmD.evidence: Reviews discuss BIRD and Spider retrieval experiments, comparisons with CORE-T, and connector-inference ablations.
24cK0fvWmD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find role-based table retrieval intuitive and recognize the distinction between useful providers, connectors, and redundant tables.
24cK0fvWmD.main_concern: Reviewers question methodological originality because complementary information, bridging tables, and the component techniques have prior precedents.

9HukJ9ruZB.one_liner: Finds minimal helpful English reasoning prefixes and distills only the missing span into target-language reasoning.
9HukJ9ruZB.problem: Models that solve English math questions can fail equivalent low-resource-language questions, while existing supervision does not locate missing reasoning spans.
9HukJ9ruZB.method: CELT progressively supplies steps from verified English reasoning to identify the smallest prefix that restores a correct target-language answer. It then matches the adapted model's target-language next-token distribution to the frozen model's English-conditioned distribution over the missing span.
9HukJ9ruZB.key_idea: Measure the minimal sufficient English reasoning prefix for each question-language pair and use it to target same-model cross-lingual distillation.
9HukJ9ruZB.evidence: Reviewers report experiments across models, benchmarks, and languages, with consistent improvements particularly in low-resource settings.
9HukJ9ruZB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the fine-grained diagnostic of missing reasoning spans and targeted supervision from the model's own English reasoning.
9HukJ9ruZB.main_concern: Frontier measurement requires substantial extra decoding, but its computational cost relative to training and achieved gains is insufficiently reported.

sqsJWJ5DII.one_liner: Low-rank curvature modeling coordinates hardware-legal FP4 scales and codes through convex relaxation and sparse fractional recovery.
sqsJWJ5DII.problem: Correlated activations couple quantization errors across groups, making independent rounding inaccurate and joint discrete optimization intractable.
sqsJWJ5DII.method: The method approximates reconstruction curvature with dense within-group blocks and a rank-r cross-group factor, then coordinates candidate scales and codes through dual optimization. Extreme-point support reduction leaves at most r fractionally mixed groups for discrete recovery.
sqsJWJ5DII.key_idea: A shared r-dimensional residual coordinates groupwise candidate mixtures, and extreme-point reduction preserves that residual while removing nearly all fractional groups.
sqsJWJ5DII.evidence: The paper proves support reduction to at most r fractional groups and reports quantization experiments using NVFP4.
sqsJWJ5DII.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the mathematical formulation and its coherent connection between low-dimensional coordination and hardware-legal FP4 recovery.
sqsJWJ5DII.main_concern: Evaluation does not establish the framework's scope across alternative quantization approaches and native formats beyond NVFP4.

uCuyWIRgFi.one_liner: Regularized probability-simplex relaxation preserves discrete one-variable local optima while enabling projected ADAM search.
uCuyWIRgFi.problem: Local minima of continuous relaxations need not correspond to locally optimal discrete assignments.
uCuyWIRgFi.method: LEMON represents each discrete variable as a probability vector and adds a regularizer promoting discrete assignments. Projected ADAM searches the relaxation before decoding and checking feasibility and local optimality.
uCuyWIRgFi.key_idea: A regularized extension on probability simplices makes continuous local minima correspond exactly to discrete local optima in the original one-variable neighborhood.
uCuyWIRgFi.evidence: The paper proves landscape equivalence and evaluates maximum independent set, graph coloring, Max-k-Cut, and k-way number partitioning.
uCuyWIRgFi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the theoretical value of preserving the native categorical neighborhood and connecting continuous minima to discrete local optima.
uCuyWIRgFi.main_concern: The theoretical and empirical advantage over closely related relaxation methods and omitted competitive baselines remains insufficiently established.

pGNL1GsV5V.one_liner: Attention-based rewards and an entropy-deviation stopping rule adapt vision-language policies on unlabeled test data.
pGNL1GsV5V.problem: Consensus-based test-time reinforcement learning can reinforce visually unsupported answers and lacks a label-free way to choose adaptation duration.
pGNL1GsV5V.method: PrimeFocus rewards image attention share, attention concentration, and attention-map concentration within answer groups. It stops when cumulative deviation of mean token entropy from its exponential moving average plateaus.
pGNL1GsV5V.key_idea: Answer-to-image attention statistics supplement consensus rewards, while a plateau in cumulative token-entropy deviation determines when adaptation stops.
pGNL1GsV5V.evidence: Experiments use three visual recognition and four visual question answering benchmarks with InternVL3-2B and InternVL2.5-4B, alongside component ablations and attention diagnostics.
pGNL1GsV5V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the concrete motivation and evidence that attention rewards contribute beyond the stopping rule.
pGNL1GsV5V.main_concern: Concentrated or shared attention is not sufficiently validated as evidence of relevant visual grounding or correction of unsupported consensus.

N9T7mUlxJ4.one_liner: Complete Path Contribution decomposes network outputs into additive path contributions and searches for the strongest pathways.
N9T7mUlxJ4.problem: Component-level attribution misses higher-order interactions and cancellation along complete input-to-output pathways.
N9T7mUlxJ4.method: Complete Path Contribution decomposes the output difference from a baseline into individual path contributions using the chain rule and Integrated Gradients. Partial summation yields complete attributions at coarser granularities, while a top-k algorithm searches for the strongest paths.
N9T7mUlxJ4.key_idea: Sum integrated contributions along complete paths, then regroup those paths to obtain consistent edge, neuron, and subnetwork attributions.
N9T7mUlxJ4.evidence: Hierarchical completeness analysis and toy-model and MNIST case studies demonstrate how strong opposing paths can cancel in component-level attributions.
N9T7mUlxJ4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the distinction between weak pathways and strong opposing pathways hidden by small net neuron contributions.
N9T7mUlxJ4.main_concern: Path rankings and cancellation conclusions lack adequate robustness checks across integration accuracy, baseline choices, and selected examples.

R3nU2XTeJv.one_liner: FLAG projects fast-task updates onto identifiable shared factors before adapting predictions for tasks with delayed labels.
R3nU2XTeJv.problem: Adapting to early labels can improve observed tasks while harming tasks whose labels arrive later.
R3nU2XTeJv.method: The framework models shifts as changing gains on shared factors with fixed task readouts and identifies which slow-task changes fast labels determine. FLAG applies a projected refit to a frozen multi-task model, removing updates in unread factor directions.
R3nU2XTeJv.key_idea: Remove update components along factors unobserved by fast tasks before transferring adaptation to slow tasks.
R3nU2XTeJv.evidence: Identification and projected-update theory are evaluated through replays on four datasets and 47 weeks of a question-answering site.
R3nU2XTeJv.claimed_gains: FLAG reports the lowest slow-task error of eight baselines and is worse than not adapting in none of 89 served windows.
R3nU2XTeJv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical fast-to-slow adaptation failure mode and the principled projection derived from identification analysis.
R3nU2XTeJv.main_concern: The fixed-factor and fixed-readout assumption restricts generality and weakens safety claims when task relationships themselves drift.

brM5cLBa3G.one_liner: RAVEL evaluates writing agents through planned outlining, drafting, reviewing, and refinement operations on reverse-engineered writing tasks.
brM5cLBa3G.problem: Final-output evaluation fails to reveal how language models perform individual synthesis operations and manage writing workflows.
brM5cLBa3G.method: RAVEL lets tester agents plan and execute outlining, drafting, reviewing, and refining while recording process behavior and final quality. C3EBench reverse-engineers professional writing into Cloze, Edit, Expand, and End-to-End tasks.
brM5cLBa3G.key_idea: Expose writing-operation choices and execution alongside final-text assessments to diagnose synthesis workflows.
brM5cLBa3G.evidence: The study evaluates 14 LLMs on 1,258 C3EBench samples and includes human assessments and controller/refiner replacement experiments.
brM5cLBa3G.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the process-level framework and complementary writing scenarios useful for diagnosing behavior missed by final-output scores.
brM5cLBa3G.main_concern: Component-replacement experiments confound reasoning, generation, instruction following, and workflow compatibility, so they do not isolate reasoning dominance.

1qoRIp9iuN.one_liner: CalTree learns conditional acceptance probabilities from target-model replays to allocate retrieved speculative draft trees.
1qoRIp9iuN.problem: Retrieval frequencies can rank sibling candidates correctly while allocating speculative trees poorly because they are miscalibrated acceptance probabilities.
1qoRIp9iuN.method: CalTree fits a 29-parameter acceptance model on annotation-free replays using retrieval and request-local features. Its scores guide tree allocation, motivated by theoretical conditions for allocation invariance and bounds on acceptance loss.
1qoRIp9iuN.key_idea: Allocate draft-tree nodes using learned conditional acceptance probabilities along root paths instead of uncalibrated retrieval frequencies.
1qoRIp9iuN.evidence: The study combines allocation-invariance theory with five-target experiments, multiple seeds, feature ablations, and transfer across Spec-Bench, HumanEval, and CanItEdit.
1qoRIp9iuN.claimed_gains: Scorer transfer changes gains by −0.2 to +0.2 points, while tuned discounts retain a median 28% of CalTree-LR's gain on HumanEval, 18% on CanItEdit, and 37% on Spec-Bench, falling below SSSD in up to 5 of 20 settings.
1qoRIp9iuN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the distinction between candidate ranking and tree allocation and the lightweight acceptance-calibration approach.
1qoRIp9iuN.main_concern: Tree-building overhead limits throughput gains, and end-to-end advantages over simpler scoring methods remain insufficiently demonstrated.

JDviATN0QC.one_liner: A target-law ambiguity radius diagnoses unsupported factor combinations and guides acquisition toward missing interaction directions.
JDviATN0QC.problem: More samples from existing support may improve marginal prediction without identifying outcomes for a specified factor combination.
JDviATN0QC.method: The paper defines the Support-Induced Composition Radius and derives an all-sample-size risk lower bound plus a conditional interaction-span certificate. Target-span acquisition greedily adds compositions that reduce the target feature's residual outside the training span.
JDviATN0QC.key_idea: Test whether a target interaction feature lies in the training row span and acquire compositions that reduce its orthogonal residual.
JDviATN0QC.evidence: Theory is supported by controlled support-expansion experiments, 200 six-factor design tasks, a UCI Bike Sharing audit, and an omitted-interaction stress test.
JDviATN0QC.claimed_gains: Three TSA additions reduce mean normalized squared target residual to 0.0023 versus 0.5057 for regularized D-optimal design, and TSA reduces average target RMSLE by 11.4% relative to the best non-targeted policy at 200 added records.
JDviATN0QC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the theoretical distinction between structural non-identification and estimation error and the controlled experiments illustrating support gaps.
JDviATN0QC.main_concern: Practical effectiveness is insufficiently validated beyond one real-world dataset and against target-specific experimental-design alternatives.

oZ5WzbDa8R.one_liner: Matched pretraining comparisons test how diffusion, masked modeling, and causal prediction affect text embeddings under limited supervision.
oZ5WzbDa8R.problem: The effect of pretraining objectives on embedding quality across downstream supervision budgets is unclear.
oZ5WzbDa8R.method: The study pretrains parameter-matched ModernBERT-style models with masked language modeling, discrete diffusion, or causal prediction on the same Ettin mixture. It compares unsupervised, frozen-backbone, and supervised adaptation across scales and tasks.
oZ5WzbDa8R.key_idea: Hold architecture, data mixture, and nominal token budget fixed while varying pretraining objectives and downstream supervision.
oZ5WzbDa8R.evidence: Models from 20M to 500M parameters are evaluated on semantic similarity, retrieval, clustering, typo robustness, BEIR, and MTEB English v2.
oZ5WzbDa8R.claimed_gains: At 500M, diffusion achieves BEIR nDCG@10 of 0.229 versus 0.217 for MLM and 0.128 for the causal model under SimCSE, and 0.250 versus 0.243 and 0.135 with 10k triplets.
oZ5WzbDa8R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled comparison across model scales, adaptation regimes, and diverse downstream tasks.
oZ5WzbDa8R.main_concern: A single architecture family, corpus, and fixed pretraining budget limit how broadly the empirical conclusions can generalize.

Bb51wk8QOo.one_liner: A shape-component kernel weight changes scale-shape curvature in sliced-Gaussian regularization while preserving the Gaussian target.
Bb51wk8QOo.problem: Standard sliced-Gaussian regularizers fix relative scale and shape sensitivity through latent width rather than a separately adjustable parameter.
Bb51wk8QOo.method: The method rescales the shape component of the analytic infinite-slice objective's kernel with one positive weight. This changes curvature while preserving positive definiteness and the minimizer, with unit weight recovering the standard objective.
Bb51wk8QOo.key_idea: Rescale only the shape component of the regularizer kernel to alter scale-shape curvature without changing its minimizer.
Bb51wk8QOo.evidence: The paper provides curvature and kernel analysis and evaluates representation rank and downstream behavior on image and time-series data.
Bb51wk8QOo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the scale-shape analysis and mathematically motivated control of representation geometry interesting.
Bb51wk8QOo.main_concern: Downstream gains are modest and inconsistent, especially for the primary time-series outcomes.

x2dgbOoftW.one_liner: Sketched correlation telemetry adaptively skips unnecessary orthogonalization corrections during randomized QR factorization.
x2dgbOoftW.problem: Maintaining explicitly orthonormal bases makes QR decomposition expensive in machine-learning pipelines.
x2dgbOoftW.method: Lazy Kernel QR uses a low-dimensional sketched kernel to monitor local basis geometry and choose orthogonalization corrections per column. Cumulative laziness controls theoretical conditioning and orthogonality bounds.
x2dgbOoftW.key_idea: Use sketched residual correlations to decide which ambient-space orthogonalization corrections each column needs.
x2dgbOoftW.evidence: Exact reconstruction and orthogonality bounds accompany evaluations in ogbn-arxiv classification, GaLore, randomized PCA, QR-LoRA, GPM continual learning, and Qwen-2.5 KV-cache compression.
x2dgbOoftW.claimed_gains: LKQR reports 4.2×–44.1× fewer orthogonalization FLOPs than MGS at no measurable downstream loss and stays within 3.2 points of the exact orthogonalizer on a continual-learning sequence.
x2dgbOoftW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard adaptive sketch-based correction as sensible and appreciate the broad application evaluation.
x2dgbOoftW.main_concern: FLOP savings are not backed by sufficient practical runtime comparisons, particularly GPU timings against other sketch-based orthogonalizers.

L79foKZdyZ.one_liner: Body-prior support assigns Gaussian avatar geometry to body-aligned or residual layers with coordinated supervision, gradients, and topology.
L79foKZdyZ.problem: A single body-guided representation forces body-supported and loose off-body surfaces to share unsuitable geometry and optimization capacity.
L79foKZdyZ.method: RRA-Avatar retains an SMPL-guided body layer and seeds a residual-surface layer from temporally fused multi-view foreground evidence. Responsibility allocation coordinates layer-specific supervision, gradient flow, and topology while allowing joint boundary refinement.
L79foKZdyZ.key_idea: Partition representation responsibility by how well the fitted body prior explains foreground geometry, then coordinate optimization across the two layers.
L79foKZdyZ.evidence: Experiments on DNA-Rendering, I3D-Human, and ZJU-MoCap assess loose-structure reconstruction with visual comparisons and allocation ablations.
L79foKZdyZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the support-based split and reconstruction improvements for loose garments and other off-body structures.
L79foKZdyZ.main_concern: Ablations do not sufficiently isolate the benefit of coordinating supervision, gradients, and topology from accompanying capacity and optimization choices.

9qhFrlcwIi.one_liner: Vocabulary-derived concept directions probe model representations to estimate answerability before generating an answer.
9qhFrlcwIi.problem: Existing answerability estimators often require answer generation or task-specific training data.
9qhFrlcwIi.method: Answerability Direction Probing constructs concept directions from vocabulary tokens in unembedding space and probes representations across layers. A Jacobian lens aligns intermediate layers, producing a score from one forward pass with a shared LLM/VLM configuration.
9qhFrlcwIi.key_idea: Project layer representations onto vocabulary-derived answerability directions, using Jacobian-based alignment for intermediate layers.
9qhFrlcwIi.evidence: Experiments cover multiple LLM and VLM families, diverse tasks, direction and robustness ablations, and a model-cascading case study.
9qhFrlcwIi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see practical value in estimating answerability before generation without training, with encouraging results across LLMs and VLMs.
9qhFrlcwIi.main_concern: The proposed three-factor decomposition is not directly validated or clearly connected to the directions actually used in the final score.

JoXajSH0vV.one_liner: Asymmetric attention adds intermediate-answer supervision to long reasoning traces without exposing auxiliary answers to the reasoning stream.
JoXajSH0vV.problem: Students distilled on complete reasoning traces struggle to answer correctly when inference budgets truncate their reasoning.
JoXajSH0vV.method: AID retains full teacher-trace supervision while training auxiliary final-answer branches from randomly sampled intermediate states. An asymmetric attention mask prevents those branches from entering the reasoning stream's forward context, with inference unchanged.
JoXajSH0vV.key_idea: Train final-answer prediction from intermediate reasoning prefixes while masking auxiliary answer tokens out of the main reasoning stream.
JoXajSH0vV.evidence: Qwen3-0.6B experiments use OpenR1-Math and KodCode, math and code benchmarks, and truncation-based evaluation of held-out validation problems.
JoXajSH0vV.claimed_gains: Under long-trace distillation, accuracy improves from 22.9% to 37.0% on MATH-500 and from 25.6% to 35.6% on MBPP+.
JoXajSH0vV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical intermediate-answer objective, reuse of existing traces, and gains for small models under long-CoT distillation.
JoXajSH0vV.main_concern: Comparisons do not isolate the asymmetric mask and intermediate-state sampling from simpler truncated-prefix or endpoint answer supervision.

pYTZDuvSBs.one_liner: Prompted video generation and 3D reconstruction synthesize paired-human object interactions for structured latent diffusion modeling.
pYTZDuvSBs.problem: Human-object-human modeling lacks scalable interaction data and otherwise depends on constrained capture or strong pose and contact assumptions.
pYTZDuvSBs.method: The pipeline combines prompt-driven video generation, SAM3D reconstruction, and geometry-aware refinement to create HOHI4D without predefined object templates. HOHI-VAE separates human motion, object dynamics, and global interaction latents for HOHI-Diff generation.
pYTZDuvSBs.key_idea: Reconstruct generated interaction videos into 3D sequences and model human, object, and global interaction factors in a structured latent space.
pYTZDuvSBs.evidence: HOHI4D contains over 5,000 sequences and 13 hours of motion, with reconstruction comparisons, generative evaluation, and component ablations.
pYTZDuvSBs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the interaction-data bottleneck and the potential usefulness of an automated, scalable synthesis pipeline.
pYTZDuvSBs.main_concern: Independent validation of synthetic 3D geometry, motion, and contact quality is missing despite visible reconstruction artifacts.

PMadTXqktt.one_liner: Observation-driven entity-channel graphs combine sparse asynchronous measurements with shared reference entities and temporal memory.
PMadTXqktt.problem: Fixed patches can split temporal dynamics, while dense or prior-based channel graphs may propagate irrelevant information in irregular time series.
PMadTXqktt.method: REA-DG connects a sample entity only to currently observed channels, using it to mediate local interactions. Shared learnable reference entities connect to all channels through channel-specific edges, supplementing sparse observations with learned context and temporal memory.
PMadTXqktt.key_idea: Mediate observed-channel interactions through a sample entity and inject shared context through learned reference entities.
PMadTXqktt.evidence: Evaluation includes four clinical datasets and two forecasting datasets with five-seed results and reported gains on P19.
PMadTXqktt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the observation-dependent architecture and promising clinical and forecasting performance.
PMadTXqktt.main_concern: The distinct advantage over existing intermediary-node and cross-channel aggregation mechanisms is insufficiently explained and demonstrated.

ls9nJ25ave.one_liner: MELT tracks relation-level taint across memory dependency graphs and checks suspicious dependencies against independent evidence.
ls9nJ25ave.problem: Memory poisoning can distribute malicious influence across individually plausible records that whole-memory detectors miss.
ls9nJ25ave.method: MELT decomposes natural-language memories into dependency relations and builds a graph spanning individual and combined memories. Relation-level taint propagation tracks untrusted influence before independent evidence validates security-relevant dependencies.
ls9nJ25ave.key_idea: Propagate provenance taint through cross-memory dependency relations and validate tainted relations rather than judging entire memory records independently.
ls9nJ25ave.evidence: Controlled-environment and AgentDojo experiments include ablations and retrieval-time evaluation of compositional memory attacks.
ls9nJ25ave.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find relation-level analysis well matched to attacks that emerge only when apparently benign memories are combined.
ls9nJ25ave.main_concern: Detection results do not establish end-to-end reductions in successful attacks while preserving benign task performance.

Vb3uGkQ6gI.one_liner: Replay schedules test stored agent-written pipelines against full-log oracles to reveal errors hidden by snapshot grading.
Vb3uGkQ6gI.problem: Pipelines that pass a single execution can silently corrupt tables when records are duplicated, delayed, reordered, or retried.
Vb3uGkQ6gI.method: The benchmark reuses each generated pipeline across delivery schedules and compares its table with an oracle recomputed from the complete record log. It separates silent table errors from crashes and tests hazard prompts and identity-based repairs.
Vb3uGkQ6gI.key_idea: Run identical stored pipeline code under multiple delivery histories and compare each resulting table with a complete-log reference.
Vb3uGkQ6gI.evidence: Evaluation spans 40 tasks and eleven models, plus 13 independently written tasks and exploratory event-identity and aggregation controls.
Vb3uGkQ6gI.claimed_gains: Snapshot pass rates are 86.0–100.0%, yet 7.0–79.2% of passing pipelines fail replay; on independent tasks, smaller models show 28.5–92.4% failure, while GPT-5.6 Sol reaches zero, Opus 5 leaves 6.2%, and Kimi K3 leaves 13.5%, with all three reaching zero after hazard hints.
Vb3uGkQ6gI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value testing the same stored code under snapshot and replay conditions, making silent temporal failures directly observable.
Vb3uGkQ6gI.main_concern: The narrow task interface and stable record identities limit real-world coverage, while explicit hints eliminate differentiation among the strongest models.

47n8P6xBu3.one_liner: Controlled feature-adaptation comparisons test whether source accuracy and adaptation granularity predict imaging-sonar transfer.
47n8P6xBu3.problem: The assumption that higher source-domain accuracy improves sonar transfer lacks controlled validation.
47n8P6xBu3.method: The study compares six adaptation schemes spanning token-level scalar adjustment, channel transformation, and global affine mapping using a 576M-parameter visual encoder. A three-backbone, three-source matrix checks whether granularity preferences change while retaining the same sonar target.
47n8P6xBu3.key_idea: Vary adaptation granularity under controlled training conditions and compare source classification with transfer to the same sonar target.
47n8P6xBu3.evidence: Experiments compare six adaptation schemes and three backbones across three source domains on one sonar classification target.
47n8P6xBu3.claimed_gains: Coarse-grained scalar adaptation achieves 96.5% transfer accuracy versus 95.1% for source-domain fine-tuning.
47n8P6xBu3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled evidence that stronger source-domain accuracy need not yield better sonar transfer.
47n8P6xBu3.main_concern: Evaluation on a single small sonar target limits statistical confidence and the generality of granularity preferences.

XZx4OGhiuz.one_liner: JUCAL fits two ensemble-calibration parameters using validation likelihood to adjust aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty contributions.
XZx4OGhiuz.problem: Standard ensemble calibration can leave the balance between label noise and model disagreement poorly represented across inputs.
XZx4OGhiuz.method: JUCAL optimizes two constants that weight and scale uncertainty contributions using negative log-likelihood on a calibration set. It operates on trained ensemble outputs without accessing internal model parameters.
XZx4OGhiuz.key_idea: Two jointly fitted scaling and weighting parameters adjust ensemble predictions through a shared validation-likelihood objective.
XZx4OGhiuz.evidence: Text-classification experiments vary tasks, datasets, ensemble sizes, pretrained networks, and ensembling strategies, with qualitative uncertainty-consistency analyses.
XZx4OGhiuz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find ensemble-aware uncertainty calibration appealing and the two-parameter method lightweight, accessible, and empirically promising.
XZx4OGhiuz.main_concern: Optimizing the averaged prediction's likelihood does not establish that aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty are individually calibrated or disentangled.

CBZwWadNFf.one_liner: ClipStore repairs clip boundaries and reuses compatible features at multiple encoder depths while preserving request-local state.
CBZwWadNFf.problem: Repeatedly encoding overlapping video clips wastes computation, but independently initialized causal encoders prevent naive reuse of source encodings.
CBZwWadNFf.method: ClipStore repairs boundaries, reuses shallow features, and switches to deeper features when dependencies and sampling phases align while keeping the remaining layers' state continuous. A request-plan optimizer selects retained positions, cuts, temporal groups, and GPU or host placement under feature budgets.
CBZwWadNFf.key_idea: Depth-dependent dependency and sampling-phase checks permit exact feature substitution while boundary repair and continuous suffix state preserve independent-encoding outputs.
CBZwWadNFf.evidence: Wan2.1 and CogVideoX implementations are checked for bitwise equality in four-video studies, with timing against fixed cuts, independent tensor batches, and Musubi's actual loader.
CBZwWadNFf.claimed_gains: Construction time falls by 9.5% and 24.7% and retained bytes by 21.9% and 31.9%, with 2.52× and 2.39× speedups over independent tensor batches and 14.2% savings with Musubi's loader.
CBZwWadNFf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the correctness analysis for exact reuse and measurements that include feature construction and output writes.
CBZwWadNFf.main_concern: Reviewers question generalization of exact reuse and cut selection beyond the narrowly tested encoder, hardware, and execution configurations.

Bte7VishUP.one_liner: Proves adding one bilinear Transformer block reduces width from quadratic to linear for quadratic in-context regression.
Bte7VishUP.problem: Quadratic in-context regression in R^d involves Theta(d^2) task coefficients, raising the question of whether Transformer depth can eliminate the need for quadratic token width.
Bte7VishUP.method: The authors analyze Gaussian quadratic in-context regression with bilinear Transformers both unrestricted and under the protected-label restriction where feed-forward layers cannot read or modify labels. They construct an explicit multi-block network that evaluates a quadratic projection-kernel estimator sequentially by applying a context-dependent attention matrix to the query using O(d)-dimensional states.
Bte7VishUP.key_idea: Evaluate a quadratic projection-kernel estimator sequentially across Transformer blocks by applying a context-dependent attention matrix to the query in O(d) states instead of storing O(d^2) features.
Bte7VishUP.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower bounds on relative risk across block depths and widths, paired with experiments reproducing the constructive risk and testing trained bilinear and GPT-style Transformers.
Bte7VishUP.claimed_gains: Reduces the token width required to achieve relative risk below one from Theta(d^2) to 3d + 5 (Theta(d)), reaching relative risk at most epsilon with O(d^2 / epsilon) context examples using two unrestricted blocks or three protected-label blocks.
Bte7VishUP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper establishes a clear, constructive depth-width separation demonstrating how sequential computation through context replaces explicit Theta(d^2) feature storage.
Bte7VishUP.main_concern: The separation relies on restrictive architectural assumptions—specifically bilinear feed-forward maps and protected labels—with limited empirical results in the main text and close overlap with prior work.

jpvGkZB40s.one_liner: Designs line-search-free AdaGrad-style adaptive step-size rules for stochastic extra-gradient variational inequalities under (delta, L)-continuity.
jpvGkZB40s.problem: Solving stochastic variational inequalities with the Extra-Gradient Method typically requires line search or prior knowledge of continuity moduli and stochastic oracle variance.
jpvGkZB40s.method: The paper develops universal, line-search-free AdaGrad-type adaptive step-size rules for the stochastic Extra-Gradient Method over compact convex sets under (delta, L)-continuity of the VI mapping. Convergence is established via an expected residual function that upper-bounds dual gaps for monotone VIs and primal-dual gaps for saddle-point and optimization problems.
jpvGkZB40s.key_idea: Adapt stochastic extra-gradient step sizes via line-search-free AdaGrad-type updates that require neither the (delta, L)-continuity modulus nor the stochastic oracle variance.
jpvGkZB40s.evidence: Theoretical convergence bounds recovering dimension-independent complexity for Holder-continuous mappings, alongside numerical experiments including l2-regression, Holder-smooth polyhedral feasibility, and softmax settings.
jpvGkZB40s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the parameter-free, line-search-free adaptive step-size design under (delta, L)-continuity and its theoretical expected-residual convergence analysis.
jpvGkZB40s.main_concern: Empirical gains over prior methods and SGD are limited or unfavorable in several tested settings, and reviewers question how substantially (delta, L)-continuity generalizes Holder continuity on bounded sets.

srDxxNcZFg.one_liner: Derives precomputed record-weighted Brier training with efficient-influence-function correction for classification under counterfactual image acquisition shifts.
srDxxNcZFg.problem: Changes in image acquisition policy can alter image-conditional class probabilities and the optimal image-only predictor even when overall image distributions and class proportions stay fixed.
srDxxNcZFg.method: Under conditional exchangeability, missing-at-random labels, and preserved historical assignment support, the paper identifies target Brier risk under a planned acquisition policy and derives an efficient-influence-function-corrected training objective. With linear conditional-risk regression on metadata, the objective reduces exactly to a Brier loss with precomputed record weights for standard gradient-based training.
srDxxNcZFg.key_idea: Correct historical Brier risk for a prespecified acquisition-policy intervention via its efficient influence function, reducing under linear metadata regression to gradient training with precomputed record weights.
srDxxNcZFg.evidence: Uniform excess-risk bound quantifying sensitivity to nuisance estimation, evaluated on simulations and a semi-synthetic Camelyon17 histopathology study.
srDxxNcZFg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing counterfactual image-acquisition shifts causally is meaningful for domains like medical imaging and yields a principled framework with practical weighted-loss optimization.
srDxxNcZFg.main_concern: Empirical validation is limited to simulations and a single semi-synthetic Camelyon17 setup using synthetic stain cues and frozen features rather than naturally occurring acquisition shifts with end-to-end training.

zbKht72pSO.one_liner: Detects wearable-sensor stroke deviations with graph-structured latent diffusion and verifies coaching feedback via knowledge-graph MLLM reasoning.
zbKht72pSO.problem: Existing wearable-sensor badminton coaching systems lack biomechanically structured modeling, preventing flagged errors and coaching feedback from being verifiably traced to specific body parts and stroke phases.
zbKht72pSO.method: Badminton Intelligent Coach (BIC) models skeletal motion, muscle activity, plantar pressure, and eye gaze with a conditional latent diffusion model organized over a biomechanical body-part-sensor graph to detect stroke anomalies. Flagged deviations are then verified against biomechanical rules in a two-level knowledge graph and converted into traceable coaching feedback by a reasoning MLLM.
zbKht72pSO.key_idea: Model multimodal wearable signals with a conditional latent diffusion model over a biomechanical body-part-sensor graph, then verify flagged anomalies through a two-level knowledge graph and reasoning MLLM.
zbKht72pSO.evidence: Evaluated on backhand drive and forehand clear strokes from the MultiSenseBadminton dataset, including component ablations and blind adjudication by four domain experts.
zbKht72pSO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the intuitive detect-then-verify pipeline, biomechanical body-part-sensor graph structure, and expert human evaluation linking sensor anomalies to traceable coaching feedback.
zbKht72pSO.main_concern: The coaching benchmark pools ground-truth errors from evaluated model outputs while giving BIC extra expert-calibrated visual references and uncapped findings relative to capped MLLM baselines, alongside requiring a lab-grade sensor suite.

RS1h0oATlt.one_liner: Tests causal psychometric validity in LLMs by editing linear emotion and mental-health activation directions during 0–100 self-rating generation.
RS1h0oATlt.problem: Strong correlation between LLM psychological self-ratings and internal concept representations does not establish whether self-ratings causally depend on those internal states.
RS1h0oATlt.method: The authors extract linear activation vectors for six emotions and six mental-health constructs from independent stories and prompt models on 24 intensity-graded scenario templates using a 0–100 self-rating scale. At the final prompt token, they edit each construct readout to match its value in the opposite-intensity scenario to test causal sensitivity.
RS1h0oATlt.key_idea: Test whether LLM psychological self-ratings causally measure internal representations by editing linear construct readouts at the final prompt token to opposite-intensity scenario values.
RS1h0oATlt.evidence: Tested across six emotions, six mental-health constructs, 24 scenario templates, and 384 readout-matching edits in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct, alongside open-ended steering checks.
RS1h0oATlt.claimed_gains: Construct readouts correlate closely with 0–100 self-ratings (mean within-template r = 0.899 and 0.791), yet across 384 opposite-intensity readout edits self-ratings never shift by more than 0.9 points against natural gaps of 30 to 41 points.
RS1h0oATlt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise combining causal measurement theory with mechanistic activation interventions in a clear, carefully controlled experimental design.
RS1h0oATlt.main_concern: All three reviewers question whether single-position, single-direction story-extracted vectors capture the specific or multi-dimensional representations models actually use when generating numerical self-ratings.

y8k9h8Kq38.one_liner: Removes a variance self-product from martingale-moment training so forecast revisions reflect news rather than smoothing.
y8k9h8Kq38.problem: Penalizing forecast-revision magnitude rewards stability instead of ensuring that revisions are unpredictable from previously available information.
y8k9h8Kq38.method: The paper turns the conditional-mean martingale restriction into an instrumented multi-horizon objective and replaces squared minibatch moments with an off-diagonal U-statistic. Moment-U removes the positive diagonal self-product that rewards low revision variance.
y8k9h8Kq38.key_idea: Estimate instrumented martingale moments with off-diagonal sample pairs, eliminating the revision-variance term hidden in naive squared moments.
y8k9h8Kq38.evidence: The authors prove population compatibility, conditional unbiasedness for shuffled finite-series batches, and an O(1/n) bias bound, then evaluate DLinear, PatchTST, and iTransformer with synthetic-news and frozen diagnostics.
y8k9h8Kq38.claimed_gains: Across PatchTST/iTransformer studies, a frozen richer kernel score falls 6.6–40.3% in all four backbone–dataset cells, with mixed MSE changes.
y8k9h8Kq38.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the distinction between stability and revision efficiency is precise and useful and that the U-statistic correction is theoretically sound and backbone-agnostic.
y8k9h8Kq38.main_concern: Reviewers question practical payoff beyond the training diagnostic and note that guarantees cover only a finite hand-designed instrument bank with little MSE change.

FUSuNqVtsV.one_liner: Pre-trains a decoupling-aware Prior-Data Fitted Network on synthetic SCMs for zero-shot Markov boundary discovery and graph reconstruction.
FUSuNqVtsV.problem: Traditional causal discovery struggles with strong nonlinearity and noise, while direct graph-prediction foundation models are underexplored for explicit structural recovery.
FUSuNqVtsV.method: DCD-PFN pre-trains on synthetic Structural Causal Models to infer sample-wise decoupling weights and predict Markov boundaries in a single forward pass, then reconstructs global CPDAGs via parallelized local discovery.
FUSuNqVtsV.key_idea: Infers sample-wise decoupling weights in a Prior-Data Fitted Network to perform zero-shot Markov boundary prediction before local-to-global causal graph reconstruction.
FUSuNqVtsV.evidence: Experiments on synthetic benchmarks and real-world datasets including Sachs, compared against baselines such as AVICI.
FUSuNqVtsV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that amortizing Markov boundary discovery via a decoupling-aware PFN for local-to-global causal reconstruction is a distinctive and well-motivated design.
FUSuNqVtsV.main_concern: Theoretical guarantees assume exact Markov boundaries rather than thresholded predictions, and the learned MB predictor is not directly compared against existing MB discovery algorithms.

4DFRtYiK77.one_liner: Optimizes continuous initial-noise logits for discrete diffusion via Gumbel straight-through estimation and soft mixing at test time.
4DFRtYiK77.problem: Non-differentiable categorical sampling blocks end-to-end gradient-based test-time reward alignment in uniform discrete diffusion models.
4DFRtYiK77.method: DDNO relaxes initial discrete noise to continuous logits, fixes intermediate randomness, and backpropagates terminal reward gradients through the reverse process using straight-through estimation and soft mixing.
4DFRtYiK77.key_idea: Relaxes initial discrete noise to continuous logits and propagates terminal reward gradients through fixed-randomness reverse steps using straight-through estimation and soft mixing.
4DFRtYiK77.evidence: Experiments on text-to-image generation (GenEval on FUDOKI) and steering text generation against search-based and step-wise guidance baselines.
4DFRtYiK77.claimed_gains: Achieves 0.94 GenEval overall accuracy on text-to-image generation.
4DFRtYiK77.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper tackles a well-motivated discrete control problem and designs an effective differentiable surrogate with convincing empirical gains.
4DFRtYiK77.main_concern: The headline 0.94 GenEval score uses the surrogate sampler rather than original decoding (0.86), and per-instance optimization against a reward raises concerns about evaluation-set overfitting.

6ZtaQsGCjM.one_liner: Finds size-adaptive GNN explanation subgraphs using a random-reference dual score and cooperative multi-edge RL pruning.
6ZtaQsGCjM.problem: Post-hoc GNN explainers struggle to determine the right explanation subgraph size per graph, either omitting key evidence or including irrelevant structure.
6ZtaQsGCjM.method: RDS-Explainer scores candidate subgraphs against random subgraphs of the same size via support and dispensability surpluses (the Dual Score) to identify just-sufficient subgraphs without a fixed budget. A Cooperative Edge Pruning RL policy removes multiple edges per step using graph-level feedback and generalizes to unseen graphs.
6ZtaQsGCjM.key_idea: Scores candidate subgraphs against random same-size references using support and dispensability surpluses, searched via a cooperative multi-edge pruning policy.
6ZtaQsGCjM.evidence: Evaluated across four molecular benchmarks (including Benzene and Mutagenicity) against fixed-budget and adaptive baselines with ablations and perturbations.
6ZtaQsGCjM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly optimizing explanation structure and per-graph size without a fixed budget addresses a practical limitation in GNN explainability.
6ZtaQsGCjM.main_concern: Reviewers question the necessity of both Dual Score terms and RL over simpler masking, note missing code, and observe that accuracy/size trade-offs are relegated to the appendix.
